articleTitle: Lung cancer detection using convolutional neural network and transfer learning
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Lung cancer has emerged as a significant cause for concern among individuals worldwide. Consequently, several nations provide financial resources and extend invitations to researchers and medical professionals to collaborate in addressing this issue. Lung cancer is a significant contributor to mortality subsequent to heart illness. The timely identification of lung cancer in its first stages has the potential to enhance patient survival rates. The use of Computer Vision is of utmost importance in the timely identification of lung cancer and the implementation of early therapeutic interventions, hence enhancing the likelihood of patient survival. The proposed deep learning model incorporates Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and transfer learning techniques, along with other image processing methods like image compression and picture enhancement. These approaches are used to analyze medical images and make correct predictions. Our study demonstrates a CNN model accuracy of 91.29% and a transfer learning accuracy of 95.9%.

articleTitle: Psi-zeta Approach for Assessing Network Efficiency in Log-Normal Fading and Spectrum Sharing Interference Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The paper introduced the Psi-zeta computation of network efficiency under a scenario of log-normal fading and spectrum sharing interferences. This model is aimed to improve different performance metrics such as throughput, Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise-Ratio (SINR), energy efficiency and finally outage probability also reducing. Simulations demonstrate that when evaluating the overall performance, Psi-zeta is superior to traditional methods by managing interference and resource allocation agilely. The results, especially under high load and heavy interference conditions, exhibit remarkable enhancements in network performance. The strong modifiability and expandability of psi-zeta show that it can be a good candidate for improving network efficiency in future wireless networks like 6G, where parameters like performance, reliability and energy efficiency are the key factors. This work has significant potential to enable the next-generation communication systems.

articleTitle: CNN-Based Analytical Approach for Liver Disease Classification and Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Liver disease is a major global health concern, and effective treatment requires an early and accurate diagnosis. Deep learning (DL) and Machine Learning (ML) techniques have been widely applied to improve disease prediction and classification. A range of models, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), and K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), were trained using the Indian Liver Patient Dataset (ILPD) from Kaggle in order to diagnose cases of liver illness. With an accuracy rate of 96.21%, precision rate of 74.76%, recall rate of 92.77%, and F1-score rate of 82.80%, the CNN model outperforms all others, demonstrating its ability to extract complex patterns for accurate categorization. Experimental results prove that Deep Learning (DL) methodologies, especially CNN, can enhance predictive power extensively compared to Machine Learning (ML) methods.

articleTitle: Automated Bone Fracture Detection in Radiographic Images Using a Fine-Tuned AlexNet Model
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Bone fractures are major medical problems requiring correct diagnosis and fast treatment for effective patient care. This paper explores the implementation of a modified AlexNet model for automated bone fracture detection utilizing radiographic X-ray images. Deep learning and transfer learning let training on a dataset of 10,580 X-ray images split into test, validation, and training sets produce a model. The AlexNet model achieved an overall accuracy of 94% with precision and recall values of 92% and 95% for non-fractured cases and respectively 96% and 94%. These tests reveal the model's degree of discrimination between non-fractured and fractured contexts. Preprocessing techniques, including data augmentation, normalization, and contrast enhancement, improved the model’s robustness and adaptability to diverse imaging conditions. Despite a minor discrepancy between training and validation accuracies, the results indicate the model’s potential to support radiologists by enhancing diagnostic efficiency and accuracy in clinical workflows. Future work aims to address current limitations by expanding the dataset, exploring advanced architectures, and integrating the model into clinical systems for real-time diagnosis. This study highlights the potential of deep learning in reducing manual diagnostic workloads and improving patient outcomes through reliable and efficient automated fracture detection.

articleTitle: ER-ADENN:Design and Implementation of EEG-based Emotion Recognition using Adaptive Dropout Enabled Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Emotion recognition is a computer science discipline and field of study that deals with the recognition of human emotions from facial expressions, text, physiological signals, and other forms of behavior. Because human emotions are complex and exhibit a wide range of expressions, emotion recognition is a difficult undertaking. The user experience of human-computer interaction can be enhanced by the application of emotion recognition. Emotion recognition, for instance, can be used to modify a computer system's interface to correspond with the user's emotional state. Emotion recognition is a promising field of research with a wide range of potential applications. As the field continues to develop, emotion recognition is likely to become more accurate and more widely used Emotion recognition based on EEG using adaptive dropout enabled neural network where the data collected from the SEED and DEAP dataset gets preprocessed using the adaptive filtering that utilized or dropped out the data for the enhancement. The time domain feature, Hjorth parameter feature, and frequency domain feature are generated by segmenting the data according to the frequencies of alpha, beta, gamma, and delta. The Adaptive dropout enabled network classifier optimized using the Harmony climbing algorithm developed on combining the Harmony search optimization and Hill climbing optimization performs the classification and boost the convergence and recognized the emotions effectively. The proposed model Harmony climbing algorithm with adaptive dropout enable neural network classifier apply on Deap dataset that enhance the performance and achieve the 94.96% accuracy, 95.05% sensitivity and 94.79% specificity on training percentage 90. On similar ways again the proposed model applies on seed dataset it will enhance the performance up to the level of 93.98% accuracy, 93.48% sensitivity and 94.66% specificity.

articleTitle: MobileNet-Based Real-Time Identification of Tomato Leaf Pathologies for Crop Health Management
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: This study introduces a MobileNet-based deep learning (DL) model for the organization of tomato leaf illnesses, to enhance automated disease detection in agricultural environments. The methodology is designed to categorise tomato leaves into four classifications: Scab, Rot, Alternaria, and Healthy. The MobileNet architecture’s lightweight and economical design guarantees excellent accuracy while minimizing computing requirements, rendering it appropriate for real-time applications in resource-constrained settings. To improve generalization and handle variability in leaf appearance, various data augmentation techniques were employed. The suggested MobileNet model achieves a remarkable accuracy of 96.02% on the tomato dataset, outperforming traditional CNN models and ensemble approaches. Future research could focus on integrating the model with IoT devices for real time monitoring and disease detection in the field and expanding the dataset with a diverse set of images. This would enable a comprehensive solution for crop health management, supporting farmers in optimizing crop yield and mitigating disease loss.

articleTitle: Leveraging Transfer Learning and Image Processing for Brain Tumor Classification from MRI Data
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: This paper presents a deep learning approach for the classification of brain tumors using MRI images, leveraging the Xception architecture for efficient and accurate detection. The dataset consisted of images related to brain tumors and healthy ones. It was preprocessed and image enhancement was done on it to improve the performance of the model. The network that was fine-tuned with transfer learning resulted in a test accuracy of about 0.989 with minor loss, indicating its good discriminative capability between the case of brain tumor and the healthy one. Evaluation of the performance by confusion matrix analysis indicates high sensitivity and specificity levels with just minor false positives and false negatives. The proposed model shows tremendous potential for real-world medical applications as it offers an automated accurate, and efficient capability of detecting the existence of brain tumors. This work provides a basis for further improvements that come in exploring different types of datasets as well as using 3D MRI scans to further improve the strength of the system. It is shown from these results that deep learning is viable as the next frontier toward improved brain tumor diagnosis: hence, more promise by this model, in early detection and subsequent reduction of workloads at diagnostic levels within clinical practice.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Framework for the Classification of Indian Heritage Using Curated Datasets and CNN Models
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The paper presents framework of image classification that uses deep learning techniques to classify monuments in India by using a very well-curated dataset that consists of 2,000 labeled images. This dataset consists of representations of landmarks that are significant, such as the Taj Mahal, Sun Temple Konark, Gateway of India, and Qutub Minar. Using TensorFlow and Keras libraries, the model was trained by an 80:20 train-test split, which used 1,600 trained dataset and 400 tested dataset of images. A simple CNN design was used, which had an few kind of convolutional layers with 32 and 64 filters, max pooling, and fully connected dense layers for classification. Data augmentation techniques such as ±20° rotatation, up to 20% zooming, and horizontal flipping were used to improve generalization, and images were altered so that pixel values were between 0 and 1. The model employed the Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 0.001 and categorical cross-entropy as its loss function. The model achieved a classification accuracy of 99.5% on the training data and 98.7% on the testing data after training for 25 epochs with a runset of 32 batches. From the loss and accuracy plots, it was seen that the model learned steadily and did not have significant overfitting. The following confusion matrix describes how predictions on new test images indicate very accurate identification of monument-specific features with only a small number of errors confirmed. The trained model can be applied practically to develop educational resources and preserve cultural heritage, and it is saved in HDF5 format. This work well shows how CNNs can recognize landmarks and can provide a strong foundation for further developments in monument classification.

articleTitle: Two Phased Methodology for Multiorgan Detection in Abdomen CT Images
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Multi-organ detection is important in medical vision field, particularly in identifying diseases and planning therapies. However, challenges such as low contrast, noise, and overlapping structures in CT images makes this task difficult. This paper focuses on addressing these challenges with a Two-Phased for Multi-Organ Detection Method (TPMMD) that proposes Efficient Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization Weighted Grey Wolf Optimization Algorithm (ECLAHE-WGWO) to enhance the CT image and X-DenseNet for precise segmentation of liver, spleen and aorta organs. The proposed technique is tested on BTCV dataset and achieves high performance with Dice scores of 96.9% for the liver, 94.23% for the aorta, and 97.73% for the spleen. These results of TPMMD show that the proposed technique outperforms those of cutting-edge techniques.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Performance of a Fine-Tuned Xception Network for Skin Cancer Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Still a major global health issue, skin cancer depends mostly on early and correct diagnosis to lower mortality rates. For medical image analysis, especially with regard to skin cancer classification, deep learning has become a transforming tool. In this work, we present an Xception-based fine-tuned deep learning model to categorize multiclass skin lesions. By means of architectural changes and transfer learning, the model was tuned to extract strong features and enhance generalization over a heterogeneous dataset. With cutting-edge methods including Swish activation, dropout regularization, and batch normalization, the network attained an accuracy of 88%. We examined training and validation performance to assess the model and observed a consistent drop in training loss while preserving a constant validation loss, hence indicating efficient learning and lower overfit. Comparative experiments demonstrated the efficacy of the fine-tuned Xception model using currently used hybrid and ensemble-based techniques such RvXmBlendNet and IncepX-Ensemble Model. Moreover, dropout layers significantly improved the generalizing ability of the network, hence addressing usual overfitting in medical data sets. This work advances automated diagnosis systems by showing the possibilities of transfer learning and optimized architectures in skin cancer detection. The suggested model presents a good tool for helping doctors classify and early detect skin lesions.

articleTitle: Early Prediction of Gastric Cancer Disorders Utilising Random Forest and Patient Lifestyle Information
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The current research focuses on the early identification of gastric cancer health-risk by using the Random Forest supervisor learning algorithm merged with patient lifestyle information’s. Gastric cancer is a leading cause of mortality worldwide, and early identification is important for improving survival rates. Traditional diagnostic methodology often fails to identify the disease at an early stage. For addressing this gap, the proposed framework integrates patient-specific lifestyle data like dietary habits, smoking frequency, alcohol intake, and daily physical activity—with a supervisor learning model to predict the likelihood of developing gastric cancer. The Random Forest Schema is used due to its robust capability to handle higher-dimensional data and capture complex relationships between lifestyle factors and cancer health risk. This model aims to assist healthcare experts in identifying higher-risk individuals, enabling timely interventions and any personalized treatment strategies. The proposed system uses the potential to improvise the effectiveness of gastric cancer screening and risk assessment depending on a combination of predictive analytics and patient behavior. The analysis results shows that Random Forest model outperforms other models in terms of accuracy (92%) and AUC-ROC (93%), while Neural Networks follow closely with an accuracy of 91%. Support Vector Machine and Logistic Regression have the lowest performance across all metrics.

articleTitle: Advancements in Brain Tumor Segmentation: A Comprehensive Review of the BraTS Challenges
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Brain tumor segmentation is a critical task in medical imaging, essential for accurate diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring of gliomas, including high-grade and lower-grade gliomas. The Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) challenges, held annually from 2017 to 2022, have significantly advanced the field by providing standardized datasets, evaluation frameworks, and fostering innovation in segmentation methodologies. In review examines the progression of BraTS challenges, highlighting key developments in data complexity, tasks, and evaluation metrics. Starting with BraTS 2017, which introduced standardized segmentation tasks and datasets with 285 subjects, subsequent iterations expanded the dataset size to 1,251 subjects by 2021 and introduced survival prediction tasks, advanced preprocessing, and enhanced segmentation algorithms. Each iteration addressed the unique challenges posed by LGG, such as diffuse boundaries and infiltrative patterns, by adopting cutting-edge architectures like 3D U-Net, nnU-Net, and Transformer-based models. These advancements have improved segmentation accuracy, robustness, and generalizability across diverse clinical settings. The review underscores the transformative role of the BraTS challenges in shaping the future of brain tumor segmentation, bridging the gap between research innovations and practical clinical applications.

articleTitle: Utilizing Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) for Apple Scab Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The research in this paper aims at evaluating a technique known as Apple Scab Disease detection using XGBoost (ASD-XG) Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) in the identification of apple scab on the apples crop which is a detrimental disease globally. The work feeds on a collection of 100 high resolution images of apple leaves on which image processing methodology is used to derive features pertinent to scab condition including color, texture and shape. The above-mentioned features of the dataset have been used to train the XGBoost model on the dataset, which showed a test accuracy of 95% as against the models like SVM, RF, CNN etc. Consequently, the experimental evaluations prove XGBoost’s higher accuracy and readability for early discovery of diseases in agriculturally important crops. The work done in this study indicates that XGBoost could underline the improvement of sustainable farming.

articleTitle: Secure Data Sharing in Financial IoT Networks Using Homomorphic Encryption and Distributed Ledger Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: This paper addresses the trade-off between network traffic and security in modern digital environments, focusing on how increased traffic affects the strength of encryption and breach rates. Realistic simulations analyze the relationship between network volume and levels of security for insight into how these challenges can be managed effectively. The results emphasize the performance versus robust security measures' balance, pointing towards advanced cryptographic techniques and scalable security solutions. This research helps in providing an understanding of this trade-off so that the optimisation of network performance goes along with high standards on data integrity and protection.

articleTitle: BanglaRoadSignNet: A YOLO-Based Framework for Efficient Road Sign Detection and Recognition in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: In developing countries like Bangladesh, the detection and recognition of road signs is a key component of intelligent transportation systems (ITS). This study addresses unique road signs and nonstandardized signage challenges, improving the detection and recognition process of traffic signs. The study highlights the increasing vehicular traffic and the lack of automation in traffic monitoring, which could improve roadway security and traffic management. This paper proposes BanglaRoadSignNet, a robust framework leveraging YOLOv11 (You Only Look Once) for accurate and simultaneous detection and recognition of road signs mainly for Bangladesh roads. BanglaRoadSignNet establishes a link between existing identification frameworks by addressing multilingual signage, occlusions, and environmental conditions, achieving high performance. The proposed model demonstrates significant performance with a precision of 94.3%, recall of 98.8%, mAP50 of 99.0%, and mAP50-95 of 92.6%, surpassing earlier versions of YOLO. The study’s major contributions are the novel architecture of YOLOv11 on a Bangladesh local dataset and its accuracy and reliability in detecting road signs, making it a practical solution for real-time ITS applications in Bangladesh.

articleTitle: Leveraging Sentinel-2 Multispectral Data and Machine Learning Algorithms for Land Use Land Cover Mapping in Semi-Arid Regions
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Land use and land cover (LULC) classification is a fundamental approach for landscape pattern mapping and monitoring of natural ecosystems and anthropogenic activities and is, therefore, an essential base for resource management to support sustainability. The land cover classes were classified in this study using multispectral data. The study utilizes Sentinel-2 data captured in February 2024, and a median composite image was generated using the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform. Three different classification algorithms, random forest (RF), classification and regression tree (CART), and naive bayes (NB), were used to produce LULC maps. The algorithms are efficient in capturing different land cover patterns with spectral diversity. The performance with essential measures such as overall accuracy (OA) and Kappa coefficient (KC) has been evaluated to assess classification outcomes. Among these classifiers, the RF classifier with the maximum OA (96.91%) and KC (96.10%) exhibited optimal results and robustness for LULC classification. CART followed this, with OA of 95.88% and KC of 94.81%. NB achieved an OA of 85.57% and KC of 81.93%. It confirms the validity of the suggested method for obtaining LULC maps through Sentinel-2 data and ML algorithms, achieving maximum accuracy in semi-arid regions.

articleTitle: Image-Based Malware Classification Powered by Deep Learning based DenseNet-121 for Enhancing Cybersecurity
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Cybersecurity is threatened by the increased number of malware and the growing emergence of sophisticated malware types. Traditional anti-malware software, commonly binarily dependent, cannot effectively cope with new and disguised threats. In this paper, authors investigate the possibility of rank-based image classification of malware using DenseNet-121 within the context of the Malimg dataset. The malware binaries introduced here are instead transformed into grayscale images: this way, the task becomes an image classification, where the model is capable of distinguishing fine features and structures which are distinctive of families of malware. DenseNet-121 uses a densely connection which enables feature propagation, reduces vanishing gradient and improves the representation learning since the features are reused at different levels. Numerous experiments on the Malimg dataset show that DenseNet-121 performs with high accuracy and is less sensitive to dataset bias than the other models in the field. The work further explores the effects of several preprocessing methods, data augmentation, and hypers parameter optimization on the model results. The results further emphasize the effectiveness of image-based analysis as a supplementary approach to malware detection, which is extendable and malleable against the emerging malicious software threats.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Systems for Collaborative Financial Decision-Making Over Distributed Network Architectures
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: In financial collaborative decision-making use case, we focus on Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) based financial decision making through distributed network architectures. The study analyses agent collaboration efficiency, system scalability, communication overhead, and decision-making accuracy through simulating different scenarios. These results show that the system adapts to varying dynamic conditions, since it continues producing high performance as the number of agents and connectivity of the network both increase. To illustrate, heatmaps and comparisons of overhead and decision texts show less communication overhead and better decisions than traditional centralized approaches can generate. The results confirm the suitability of MAS for complex financial target patterns, thus providing a scalable, efficient and robust solution for the next generation of financial decision support systems. These findings help extend MAS-inspired approaches to distributed, high-stakes decision making environments.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Networks for Analysing Social Media Data to Improve Disaster Response and Crisis Management
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Disasters, both natural and man-made, present formidable challenges to response and management activities. The development of social media has led to the creation of vast volumes of real-time data, which offer helpful insights for efficient crisis management. The data, however, is unstructured and noisy, and extracting meaningful information is challenging. This study investigates the application of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in social media data analysis to improve disaster response and crisis management. Utilizing the potential of deep learning, specifically CNNs, this study focuses on classifying posts related to disasters from various social media platforms. The paper elaborates on the data collection process, preprocessing methods, CNN model architecture, and evaluation metrics. Experimental result confirm that the CNN model is superior to traditional Machine Learning (ML) techniques in terms of efficiency and accuracy. The suggested model achieved an accuracy of 96.13%, precision of 92.08%, recall of 90.25%, and F1-score of 95.16%. The study identifies the potential of CNNs in real-time disaster response systems and provides suggestions for future enhancements in utilizing AI-driven solutions for crisis management.

articleTitle: WaveFilter: Advanced Imaging for Marine Microplastic Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: YOLOv5 has proven to be an efficient deep learning model for the detection of microplastics in aquatic environments. It is compact, with a total number of 214 layers and 7,022,326 parameters, while its model size is approximately 14.4 MB. Extensive performance analysis was done that states that the model has a precision of 79.8% and a recall of 67.1%, hence proving efficiency in the detection of instances of microplastics. The performance metrics are that the model offers a mAP of 72.1% at IoU=0.5 and averaged mAP of 34.1% averaged across different IoU values. These also validate the strength of YOLOv5 to detect microplastic with complex backgrounds which could be applied to real-time, automated, computer vision-based frameworks for the detection of marine plastic pollution. These promising results from the study have opened further vistas for development in environment monitoring and conservation.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning approach for Alzheimer’s Disease Stage Classification by integrating 3D CNN with Multi-modal inputs
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: This research concentrates on approaches to analysing the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) dataset. It utilises transfer learning across multiple 3D convolutional neural networks, drawing on pre-trained weights from ImageNet. The primary focus lies in integrating 3D neuroimaging data alongside subject-specific data such as gender, age, and visit month, all available in the ADNI dataset. The outcomes of these models are compared with single modal models and complex models, such as vision transformer model trained on 2D images generated by selecting the middle slice of the 3D images. Our multimodal 3D models performed remarkably well, with ResNet-18 being the most effective of the four models with an accuracy of 98.75%. SResNeXt-101 showed greater accuracy with multimodal (95%) over single-modal (67.26%). Our suggested multimodal architecture significantly improved the detection results compared to previous research. This study enhances early AD detection by using deep learning and multimodal data for diagnosing complex neurological disorders.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition from Speech Signals Using Hybrid CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The fast growth of internet and communications networks has drastically enhanced data transport, allowing tasks like Speech Emotion Recognition (SER), an essential aspect of human-computer interaction, to be carried out. However, it is still challenging to recognize emotions in speech due to the dynamic and varied nature of speech signals. This work proposes a hybrid Machine Learning (ML) model integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks based on enhancing the performance of SER. The CNN extracts the spectral features of the signal while the LSTM is capable of learning temporal dependencies in speech signals. Preprocessing involves the application of spectrograms and mel-frequency cepstral coefficients. Experiments performed on a public data set have revealed that the suggested hybrid model performs better than the CNN and LSTM models, with an impressive accuracy of 95%.The experimental results are promising for its applications in surveillance, autonomous driving, action recognition, and human-computer interaction.

articleTitle: Blood Group Identification by Analyzing Fingerprints using ResNet-50
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: In the domain of medical diagnostics, identification of blood groups accurately and efficiently is essential for various clinical procedures, including transfusions and organ transplants. Traditional invasive procedures involve taking a blood sample from individuals, which can be uncomfortable and may cause infections. Additionally, testing blood samples in the laboratory is time-consuming. The present approach proposes a non-invasive method for blood group identification using deep learning and fingerprint images. Fingerprints are unique patterns found on our fingertips that help in identifying individuals. By using these unique and unchangeable features of fingerprints, every individual’s blood group can be identified. The proposed approach leverages deep learning model ResNet-50, which is well known for its significance in image classification, to predict blood groups efficiently. The model achieved an accuracy of 88%, confirming its effectiveness in blood group identification. This approach addresses a critical need in the medical community, providing a seamless and technologically advanced solution for blood group identification

articleTitle: Neurodegenerative Disease Alzheimer's and Parkinson's Classification with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Computer-aided devices and systems have become increasingly common in healthcare. These devices and systems contribute significantly to the faster and earlier diagnosis of diseases. Imaging devices, especially Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Computed Tomography (CT), play a major role in diseases where early diagnosis is crucial. In neurological disorders, the use of MRI and CT images as input data in deep learning models is becoming increasingly widespread. In this study, MRI images from the "Alzheimer Parkinson 3 Class Data Set" available on the Kaggle platform were used for the diagnosis of Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases. The dataset includes three classes: 2,561 Alzheimer's, 906 Parkinson's, and 3,010 Control (Normal) images. In this work, the Alzheimer, Parkinson, and Normal classes were trained using ResNet-18, VGG-16, and ConvNext architectures, yielding accuracy rates of 96.2%, 95.4%, and 98.9%, respectively. Additionally, Alzheimer and Parkinson diseases were tested against the normal class using binary classifiers. For the Alzheimer-Normal and Parkinson-Normal classes, the models achieved the following results: ResNet-18 with accuracy rates of 82.0% and 96.1%, VGG-16 with 95.4% and 89.4%, and ConvNext with 99.4% and 99.5%, respectively.

articleTitle: Word Level Ethiopian Sign Language Recognition Using Hybrid CNN-LSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: In this research, we propose a hybrid CNN and LSTM model for word-level Ethiopian sign language recognition. The recognition system has four major components: preprocessing, feature extraction, sequence modeling, and training. Image frame extraction was performed on the collected word video dataset, followed by keyframe selection using the k-means clustering algorithm. Image concatenation and image resizing were applied to the selected keyframe images. The final dataset is downsized into 1500 images, which is 150 images for each class. CNN was utilized to extract the important features through convolutional layers, pooling layers, and dropout functions were used to overcome overfitting issues. Following feature extraction, sequence modeling was performed by using LSTM with LSTM layers, a dense layer, and a SoftMax classifier to recognize words in both predicted and actual classes. The system was tested by the dataset that we collected for this purpose. The experiment demonstrates that the proposed hybrid CNN-LSTM model performs well across the training, validation, and testing phases, achieving 98%,97%, and 95% accuracy during model evaluation, respectively. These results demonstrate the recognition success of the model isolated word-level Ethiopian sign language, which plays a step forward in assisting hearing-impaired individuals.

articleTitle: Graph Attention Network and Graph Convolutional Network for Classification of Dengue Virus Variants
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Dengue fever is a serious global health concern, particularly in warm regions where it causes significant morbidity and mortality. Dengue symptoms range from mild fever to severe hemorrhagic complications and are caused by four serotypes (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, and DENV-4), with several infections increasing the likelihood of severe results. The proper classification of Dengue virus variations is critical for vaccine development, public health policies, and treatment optimization.This article provides a new approach for categorizing Dengue virus variations that employs Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) and Graph Attention Networks (GATs). The graph built using k-mers and k-nearest neighbors, processed with the GAT model, achieved a 99.75% classification accuracy, outperforming existing methods.

articleTitle: AI-driven Data Analytics for Cyber Threat Intelligence and Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Cyber threats are evolving rapidly, making traditional malware detection approaches insufficient in handling sophisticated attacks such as zero-day exploits, polymorphic malware, and advanced persistent threats. As a solution to these problems, this study presents a novel hybrid AI-based data analysis framework for cyber threat intelligence and anomaly detection. We specifically proposed a model that combines autoencoders, random forests, and CNN-LSTM architectures to improve anomaly detection and classification. The dataset used for training and evaluation is the Microsoft Malware Dataset, a publicly available dataset. The AE-RF module learns the normal behavior of the system to detect abnormal behavior, and the CNN-LSTM model identifies spatial and temporal properties of malware for execution patterns. This article ensures that the dataset is well-preprocessed, including feature extraction, PCA, and SMOTE for class balancing to provide optimal model performance. The experimental results show that AE-RF has an area under curve (AUC) score of 0.91 and CNN-LSTM has 0.94, which demonstrates that unsupervised and supervised techniques together have high classification accuracy. This hybrid approach not only improves malware detection accuracy but also enhances cyber threat intelligence by providing interpretable insights into attack patterns. The study concludes that integrating multiple AI techniques can significantly improve cybersecurity defenses against evolving threats, paving the way for real-time, AI-powered malware detection solutions.

articleTitle: Prevention of Prompt Injection Attacks Over Financial Applications Integrated with LLM
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Prompt injection is a growing concern in financial applications integrated with Large Language Models. These attacks pose a critical risk to financial applications leading to data breaches, confidential data loss and financial losses by manipulating input prompts to cause unintended or harmful outputs. Existing defense strategies include utilizing filters f or input and output, and delimiters, however, these techniques have been proven inadequate. This paper builds upon existing mechanisms and proposes an enhanced security system that incorporates role-based access, jailbreak attack detection, validating inputs and securely passing prompts to LLM. This is done by developing a pre-processing layer at both ends-the client and LLMs-through the identification of critical as well as destructive keywords. The experimental results show that blocking of that malicious prompt ensures that only authenticated and authorized commands are processed. The measures, therefore, allow financial institutions to significantly reduce the probability of prompt injection attacks besides increasing data protection and confidence i n AI-based financial applications.

articleTitle: Audio-Based Medicine Recognition for Illiterate People using YOLOv9 Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Illiteracy is a significant barrier in solving personal healthcare problems and avoiding risks. Illiterate people cannot read labels of the prescribed medicines, and this increases the risk of medication misuse and the health risks. To address this concern, an innovative system is proposed which detects the medicine names from the user’s input images using YOLOv9 (You Only Look Once) object detection algorithm. On detection, the system provides the audio and text description of the uses of the detected medicine in the regional language (here, Marathi) of the user, making it highly accessible to an illiterate individual. Additionally, if the user inquiries about the potential side-effects of the detected medicine, the system responds with an audio explanation in Marathi, using Google’s text to speech library (gTTS) in the Python programming language. A user- friendly platform is developed using ‘Gradio’ for the deployment of the system model, this allows seamless interaction, even for users with limited technical knowledge. Notably, the model has achieved a highest mAP (mean Average Precision) of 99.5% for several commonly used medicines. The system empowers illiterate or semi-literate individuals, particularly beneficial in rural areas where the illiteracy rate is very high, to take care of their personal healthcare problems in their native language.

articleTitle: Exploring Behavioral Patterns for Security in Cloud Computing: a Case Study
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The Internet has now become a powerful enabler to access data and services offered on cloud platforms. Ensuring the security of cloud services for customers leveraging it is a challenge. The use of passwords, OTPs, certificates, biometrics, Multi-factor, OpenID, Kerberos, challenge-response, and behavioral-based authentication techniques is in use in the industry. Habit, which is a behavior that becomes automatic and is repeated often, with little to no thought, while interacting with the environment is recordable due to smart electronic gadgets. These can record the user interactions in logs using different software applications that can be analyzed and then used for providing safety in a cloud computing environment. The patterns of interest include time of login, likes, dislikes, comments, keystroke speed, errors in typing, reading, and comprehension, use of different types of devices, machines used to access the internet, trends, search phrases, reading types of news feeds can be explored for possible enhancement of security. This paper is focused on exploring the use of reading, comprehension, and typing behavioral patterns of the users to provide proactive threat-driven security while accessing cloud applications. It is the first step towards analyzing the behavioral patterns that can be used to re-authenticate the users for enhanced security of devices, applications, and services like cloud computing. The simulations tested the system’s ability to differentiate between fake and pivot users as group size is increased. While accuracy was 100% for smaller groups upto 30, it slightly decreased to 97.5% and 94% for larger groups with 2 to 4 pivot users and total of more than 40 users in all. The study is useful to minimize the malicious users’ access to services meant for the valid intended users of cloud computing.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised Learning for Anomaly Detection in IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Due to the fast growth of the IoT, security challenges are rising notably in anomaly detection. Traditional supervised learning techniques heavily depend on labeled datasets, which are often rare and become outdated as cyber adversaries evolve. Unsupervised learning is very powerful but produces high false-positive rates and lacks context. To overcome these limitations, this study presents a self-supervised learning structure for detecting anomalies in IoT networks. Utilizing contrastive learning, autoencoders, and transformers, the model derives useful representations from unlabeled data, elevating detection accuracy whilst minimizing reliance on manual labels. With the TON_IoT dataset, our proposed model outperforms traditional supervised and unsupervised methods, achieving 0.94 accuracy, 0.93 precision, and an AUC-ROC of 0.96. The outcomes illustrate the ability of self-supervised learning to improve cybersecurity in dynamic IoT environments.

articleTitle: Scalable Explainable AI with a Cloud-Native Approach for Cybersecurity Threat Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The growing complexity and number of cyber threats call for sophisticated detection approaches that provide both high performance and interpretability. The proposed hybrid AI approach (AE-RF-CNN-LSTM) is a promising hybrid up-to-date improving SEO framework for cybersecurity. All these models play a steady role in performance improvement. Autoencoders are trained to sense patterns from normal data to assist in anomaly detection, random forests help with the robustness of the model with overfitting reduction, and CNN-LSTMs assist greatly in recognizing the complex temporal dependencies in network traffic data. Experimental results show that this approach achieves substantially improved accuracy nearest neighbor anomaly detection and surpasses every single model in terms of accuracy. This hybrid framework, thus, helps to detect known and unknown cyber threats, leading to a huge decrease in false positive and false negative rates. Furthermore, integrating explainable AI (XAI) methods, including SHAP (SHapley Additive explanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations), to enhance decision interpretability. The methods enable security analysts to comprehend the most relevant features of making predictions and, therefore, trust the model and correct further cybersecurity actions. This not only allows for the improvement of defense mechanisms against cyberattacks but also builds confidence in AI-driven security solutions by providing interpretability and assurance of performance.

articleTitle: Phishing Detection in Dynamic Environments Using Network Behavior
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Phishing is a growing cybersecurity threat, prompting the need for effective detection systems. This study introduces a deep learning framework that combines CNN, LSTM, and Transformer layers to identify phishing websites by analyzing URL features such as URL and domain lengths, the inclusion of an IP in the domain, TLD, HTTPS presence, and character ratios. The CNN model reached an accuracy of 93%, the LSTM model obtained 85%, and the Transformer model surpassed both with an accuracy of 99%, a recall of 100%, and an F1 score of 99%. The proposed layered model achieved 97% accuracy, proving its effectiveness in detecting phishing websites. By incorporating CNN, LSTM, and Transformer layers, the model captures sequential relationships and emphasizes important data trends, providing a powerful tool for phishing detection and enhancing online security.

articleTitle: An Efficient Weed Detection using Adaboost and CNN Hybrid Model
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The detection of weeds is an essential component of precision agriculture because it provides farmers with the tools necessary to efficiently manage and control weed infestation in agricultural areas. Manual work is laborious and error-prone in traditional weed-detecting methods. Computer vision and machine learning have shown promise in automating weed detection in recent years. This study introduces a hybrid model that combines AdaBoost and CNN to detect weeds. The hybrid model uses AdaBoost and CNN to boost weed detection accuracy. AdaBoost is used as a feature selector to identify input images with discriminative properties. CNNs, or convolutional neural networks, are popular deep learning models that can extract complex spatial features from images. This CNN receives the selected features. The CNN learns and improves features, enabling precise weed classification. A large dataset from Kaggle with crop field images of various weed species and backdrops is used to evaluate the hybrid model. The dataset is hand-annotated to provide ground truth labels for training and testing. The dataset trains the hybrid model, which is optimized for precision, recall, and F1 score. Experimental comparisons show that the proposed AdaBoost and CNN hybrid model outperforms individual models and other weed detection methods in accuracy and computing economy.

articleTitle: Toward Entailment Checking: Explore Eigenmarking Search
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Logic entailment is essential to reasoning, but entailment checking has the worst-case complexity of an exponential of the variable size. With recent development, quantum computing when mature may allow an effective approach for various combinatorial problems, including entailment checking. Grover algorithm uses Grover operations, i.e., selective phase inversion and amplitude amplification to address a search over unstructured data with quadratic improvement from a classical method. Its original form is intended to a single-winner scenario: exactly one match is promised. Its extension to multiple-winner cases employs probabilistic control over a number of applications of Grover operations, while a no-winner case is determined by time-out. Our study explores various schemes of “eigenmarking” approach. Still relying on Grover operations, but the approach introduces additional qubits to tag the eigenstates. The tagged eigenstates are to facilitate an interpretation of the measured results and enhance identification of a no-winner case (related to no logic violation in entailment context). Our investigation experiments three variations of eigenmarking on a two-qubit system using an IBM Aer simulator. The results show strong distinguishability in all schemes with the best relative distinguishabilities of 19 and 53 in worst case and in average case, respectively. Our findings reveal a viable quantum mechanism to differentiate a no-winner case from other scenarios, which could play a pivot role in entailment checking and logic reasoning in general.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep Learning and SVM Approach for Accurate Nail Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Nail diseases, such as fungal infections, melanomas, and psoriasis, affect millions of people globally, and their accurate diagnosis is critical for timely treatment. Though these might be subjective and time-consuming for dermatologists, we propose a hybrid approach, in this paper, based on a deep learning model and a machine learning algorithm, for the automatic classification of nail diseases. A deep convolutional neural network, VGG16 CNN, is used as the feature extractor and combined with a Support Vector Machine SVM classifier. This research dataset is a collection of nail images categorized into six classes, namely Acral Lentiginous Melanoma, Healthy Nail, Onychogryphosis, Blue Finger, Clubbing, and Pitting. The VGG16 model, pretrained on ImageNet, extracts the high-level features from the nail images. These features are passed to the SVM classifier for the final classification. Extensive experiments are performed on the nail disease dataset, and the proposed model finally achieves a test set accuracy of 94.36%. The results prove the effectiveness of a combination with VGG16 for feature extraction and SVM for classification, in contrast to the performance of stand-alone deep learning models. This approach uses transfer learning and classical machine learning to efficiently and accurately construct a system for classifying nail diseases. A model developed with this system may be used as a tool for dermatologists that would help in reducing the time and effort spent on diagnosis.

articleTitle: Evaluating New Malware Trends Using Cyber Threat Intelligence Data
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The emergence of new malware attacks and other cyber threats in the digital age poses a serious cybersecurity threat; using a wealth of cyber threat data, this article thoroughly examines newly emerging malware threats, revealing these nasty programs' most recent patterns and traits. This study evaluates malware's potential hazards to several sectors, such as banking, healthcare, and critical infrastructure, by analyzing the techniques utilized for malware dissemination, evasion, and activation. The study emphasizes the significance of timely and accurate threat intelligence by integrating insights from case studies, real-world incidents, and expert analyses. The results highlight the necessity of sophisticated detection methods, strong mitigation plans, and multinational collaboration to successfully tackle the constantly changing terrain of malware threats. A comparative evaluation of precision among the Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and Decision Tree algorithms showed that the Random Forest is more accurate, and it has been observed that accuracy is 95.07. This higher accuracy depicts its ability to handle complex datasets effectively and with stability. This study adds to the current conversation on cybersecurity by providing practical suggestions for strengthening defenses and boosting resistance to malware attacks in the future.

articleTitle: PacketEye (Automated sniffer and Data Analytics)
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: A tool called a packet sniffer is used to intercept and examine network traffic, which is crucial for contemporary network security and monitoring. This study presents a unified packet sniffing solution that can capture and analyze TCP, DNS, and HTTP traffic and more, whereas traditional research mainly concentrated on particular protocols or restricted applications. Clear graphs are used to display traffic trends after the tool aggregates packet data into 1-minute intervals. For instance, power fluctuations peak at approximately 1500 seconds, while packet rates stabilize at 800 packets per minute. This method improves visibility and security by increasing the effectiveness and efficiency of real-time monitoring and traffic analysis.

articleTitle: Cost-Efficient Task Scheduling in Cloud-Fog Systems using Hybrid Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Workflow scheduling in cloud-fog environment aims to optimize task allocation, execution time, and resource management. The complexity and dynamic nature of tasks and resources make finding an optimal workflow scheduling algorithm challenging. To address these limitations, this study introduces a Hybrid Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm-Whale Optimization Algorithm (HPWOA). While Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) struggles with slow convergence and high-dimensional search spaces, Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) faces difficulties in irregular search spaces and inconsistent convergence rates. By integrating PSO and WOA, HPWOA mitigates local optimization issues and enhances optimisation efficiency. The primary objective of this work is to minimise Total Execution Cost (TEC). To validate HPWOA, a comparative analyses against PSO, WOA, and HPWOA across three scientific workflows with increasing test cases has been performed. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm is 1.92% better than PSO and 9.60% better than WOA in terms of TEC. The paper highlights HPWOA's effectiveness in improving workflow scheduling and identifying the optimal workflow configurations for cloud-fog environments.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis of Error Propagation in Hindi-English Cascaded Speech-to-Speech Translation Models
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Speech-to-Speech Translation (S2ST) plays a crucial role in reducing language barriers and enabling seamless communication between people from different linguistic backgrounds. Traditional S2ST systems typically rely on a cascaded design, where components like Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Machine Translation (MT), and Text-to-Speech (TTS) work together in sequence to complete the translation process. Cascaded models are widely used S2ST models and are prone to error propagation (EP) across the pipeline, significantly impacting translation quality. EP is discussed in various literature. However, a comprehensive quantitative analysis is not available, particularly for low-resource languages like Hindi and English. This work presents a detailed quantitative study of EP in Hindi-English cascaded S2ST models, bridging this critical research gap. This study utilizes both text-based and textless evaluation metrics such as BLEU, Translation Edit Rate (TER), and BLASER score for translation accuracy to quantify the impact of EP at various stages of the pipeline on the FLEURES dataset. The result analysis shows that due to EP, the translation quality of the S2ST model decreases in BLEU score of 11.55 for English→Hindi and BLEU score of 12.16 for Hindi→English. Similarly, reference-based BLASER decreases by 0.61 and 0.45 for English→Hindi and Hindi→English, respectively.

articleTitle: Improved Multi-Scale Object Detection Accuracy on Battery Chicken Coop with YOLO and Features Pyramid Network
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: This research aims to increase object detection accuracy in chickens in a battery cage environment with various obstacles, such as feeding places, drinking places, and iron cages. The algorithm used is You Only Look Once (YOLO), which was modified by adding a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) and several additional layers to increase detection accuracy. Images were annotated using Label Studio, and data augmentation was performed using Albumentations with a total of 29,060 annotations. The dataset was taken from livestock pens in the North Sulawesi region, Indonesia. Adjustment of the spatial size of the tensor is carried out using a forward mechanism using the F.interpolate function with the nearest neighbor method.The research results show that the YOLO modification with FPN produces a mean Average Precision (mAP) value of 0.88567, better than standard YOLO with mAP of 0.87616. Experiments were carried out on various numbers of epochs (25, 50, 75, and 100) with the best results at the 100th epoch, achieving a precision of 0.85876, recall of 0.80472, mAP50 of 0.88567, and mAP50-90 of 0.59254. In addition, a comparison is made between the proposed method and the YOLOv8 standard. The results show that YOLOv8 + FPN has precision advantages in all evaluation metrics over standard YOLOv8, especially in the values mAP50 and mAP50-90, with an increase in mAP of 4.83%.This research proves that adding FPN and additional layers to YOLOv8 effectively increases object detection accuracy in a chicken coop environment with multi-scale conditions and object obstacles. These findings significantly contribute to the development of computer vision-based object detection technology.

articleTitle: Alzheimer Disease Classification Using Custom CNN and a Hybrid Model of DcGAN with ResNet101
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) significantly impacts daily life, and manifest symptoms like memory loss, difficulty in problem-solving, confusion, language challenges, and changes in mood or personality. As the disease develops, these symptoms interrupt everyday tasks, impair relationships, and ultimately undermine independence. The suggested technique compares the outcomes of custom CNN model with a hybrid model of Deep Convolutional GAN (DcGAN) and Resnet101 model in a multi-stage manner. 1,125 labeled samples covering various stages of AD are included in the dataset, which was gathered from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) available on Kaggle. To tackle data shortage problem, synthetic images are generated with the DcGAN. The custom CNN framework is subsequently adjusted for AD classification by integrating these images with the actual ADNI dataset. The model is assessed using performance measures including accuracy, recall, precision, F1-score and validation accuracy. 90.6% accuracy is shown overall and demonstrates the model's ability to solve issue with data shortage by highlighting its competence in both generating along with classification tasks. This paper concludes by highlighting the prospects for furthering clinical processes and research on AD in the upcoming future.

articleTitle: BioTwinNet: Dual-Stream Multilevel Feature Fusion for Classification of SARS-CoV-2 and Influenza Virus Variants via Genomic Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The fast evolution and high transmissibility of emerging infectious illnesses like Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 pose serious public health problems. In order to effectively classify SARS-CoV-2 and Influenza variations, this study presents BioTwinNet, a unique dual-stream deep learning framework that integrates multilevel feature fusion with genomic image processing. Using methods like Wavelet Analysis, Discrete Cosine Transform, and Power Spectral Density, DNA sequences were converted into visual representations. BioTwinNet, which makes use of the depth capabilities of ResNet architectures and the hierarchical feature extraction of Convolutional Neural Networks, was used to evaluate these genomic images. By using Discrete Cosine Transform-Power Spectral Density characteristics, this method achieves an impressive classification accuracy of 97.42%, overcoming the difficulties caused by differences in sequence length.

articleTitle: Web-based Plant Leaf Disease Detection and Prescription Module
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Plant disease (PD) is a persistent issue for farmers that reduces both their income and food production. Even for subject matter specialists, it might be challenging to stop the disease from scattering to other portions of the plant once it has begun. Although it takes time and requires a close inspection of the sick region, experts may identify and diagnose the ailment. Smallholder farmers do not have simple access to these experts while constituting a major section of our nation. To identify the plant leaf disease and to evaluate its phases, a proper approach is thus required. Thanks to the present internet revolution and advancements in computer vision models, computer vision can now be used in agriculture. Recently, the Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) are regarded as the most advanced method for classifying pictures and are capable of making a conclusive diagnosis. To diagnose the illness using a web-based application module created using deep learning techniques through the Transfer Learning approach is used in this research paper. A pre-trained method is built on photos of diverse plant leaves from the Plant Village dataset. Various efficiency metrics such as f1-score, Precision, accuracy, recall calculations and tracking are simulated to validate the efficiency of the suggested approach. The accuracy of ResNet50 with the Plant Village Dataset was around 97.5%, and it will provide information on the disease spread level on the scanned leaf. This study will improve farming practices for producing food and reduce early-stage crop loss.

articleTitle: Optimizing AI Model Training Costs with Stratified Sampling and Self-Adaptive Testing
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The data processing and generation of datasets which are required for training Large Language Models (LLMs) and Generative AI (GenAI) applications have become costly these days. This paper presents an approach to optimize the cost of generating model training datasets by combining a stratified sampling algorithm integrated with a self-adaptive, comprehensive test suite framework. The methodology proposed in this paper will reduce the size of training datasets without impacting model performance and data integrity. This helps to reduce the cost of AI model training. Our empirical analyses demonstrate that our proposed approach reduces the cost of generating datasets up to 60%, without losing model accuracy and performances. It provides a way for efficient use of compute and storage resources for generation of high quality datasets for AI model training.

articleTitle: Enhancing Partner Query Resolution: Leveraging AI for Smart Corporate Operations
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: This research aims to develop an AI-powered chat-bot designed to support internal teams within the organization, it is responsible for managing and addressing queries related to the management of external collaborators, referred to as ’partners’, who play a critical role in the organization’s business ecosystem. Queries typically encompass partner onboarding, classification into operational tiers (gold, platinum, silver, registered), and administrative processes such as contract management, rebate registration, and accreditation. The need for this solution arises from the high volume of repetitive and actionable queries, which are 51% of the total queries received from internal teams. Currently, these queries require manual processing, consuming substantial time and resources, leading to inefficiencies and potential delays in communication. The system is centered around semantic search capabilities using ChromaDB and the Llama-3 model, streamlines query handling by automating responses to frequently asked questions. It empowers internal teams to efficiently manage partner-related interactions, reducing reliance on manual efforts while ensuring consistency and accuracy. It features a user-friendly interface, enabling seamless access for non-technical users. Initial implementation and testing demonstrated over 90% accuracy in resolving queries. This automation reduces the operational burden, enhances decision-making, and ensures real-time assistance for internal teams.

articleTitle: Enhancing Timetable Scheduling Efficiency with a Firefly Algorithm-Based Automated System: A Case Study of Landmark University
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: A timetable is an organized structure that allocates people and resources, such as classrooms, into time objects for specific events. The manual methodology of creating a timetable is a tedious and complex task that is subject to human error. These errors lead to backtracking, which could restrict the administrators from attaining the optimal solution. The objectives of this work are to design a web-based scheduling interface that generates timetables and to implement a web-based scheduling interface that generates timetables utilizing an evolutionary algorithm using front-end and back-end technologies. This study is limited to implementing a scheduling system that tries to automatically cater for each restriction involved in generating timetables. The timetables are created automatically using a firefly algorithm. The Automated Timetable System was tested in the academic setting of Landmark University, and the results were compelling in terms of time savings, increased overall efficiency, decreased scheduling efforts, improved resource utilization, and increased satisfaction for the timetable administrator. The system was capable of generating timetables using the available data stored in the database. In conclusion, the integrated automated timetable scheduling system proved to be a beneficial tool for educational institutions, improving schedule quality, decreasing effort, and maximizing resource usage. Utilizing the Firefly Algorithm allows for efficient exploration of the problem space and delays convergence to almost ideal solutions.

articleTitle: Leveraging Cloud-Native Data Engineering for Big Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Recent evolution of traditional ETL systems into a cloud-native data engineering design for big data analytics capable of elastic and low-cost scaling. The proposed pipeline combines Apache Spark on Kubernetes, AWS Glue, and Delta Lake by leveraging microservices, containerization, serverless computing, and distributed orchestration. Based on the Taxi Trip dataset, the framework allows up to several times reduction in query execution time, processing throughput, and cost efficiency as compared to typical ETL approaches. Thus, the experimental results show that the query response is 75.9% faster and the cost is reduced by 64.5%. This research highlights the advantages of cloud-native architectures in maximizing real-time analytics and details in future work auto-scaling driven by AI and hybrid edge-cloud models.

articleTitle: Animal Species Classification Using Fine-Tuned ResNet152V2: A Deep Learning Approach for Biodiversity Conservation
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Especially in challenging fields like animal species identification, deep learning methods CNN have greatly advanced image categorization. Ten different animal species Butterfly, Cat, chicken, cow, dog, elephant, Horse, sheep, spider, and squirrel, are classified using ResNet 152V2, a deep CNN architecture, in this work. The work uses class weighting, data augmentation, and transfer learning to handle class imbalance so enhancing the the model ability to generalise. A validation accuracy of 88% results from fine-tuning the ResNet 152V2 model to maximize accuracy and economy. With an eye toward minority groups like elephants, the classification performance was fully assessed utilizing precision, recall, and F1-scores. Consistent progress without overfitting indicated the robustness of the model by means of the examination of training and validation loss and accuracy. By proving the possibilities of deep CNNs in uses like wildlife monitoring, biodiversity preservation, sustainable development, ecosystem preservation, and environmental resilience, this research supports long-term conservation efforts and responsible use of natural resources so contributing to the field of image classification.

articleTitle: Culinary Classification with Deep Learning: A Study of Pandang Cuisine Using MobileNetV3
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Rich tastes, varied ingredients, and visually beautiful feasts define Pandang cuisine. Still, Pandang food is difficult to separate from its seeming homogeneity and professional cooking techniques. Apart from other purposes, computerized classification of these items would be especially beneficial for meal delivery, restaurant automation, nutritional monitoring, and cultural preservation. Accurate food recognition systems help to maintain traditional recipes, thereby enhancing nutritional monitoring, inventory control, food waste reduction, and culinary tourist support. Including depth wise separable convolutions and squeeze-and-excitation modules into MobileNetV3's optimal architecture provides outstanding accuracy with minimal computational cost, which fit for real-time applications on mobile and Edge devices. To improve model performance, this work used a 993 Kaggle picture dataset applying data preprocessing, augmentation, and a fine-tuning technique. Training, validation, and testing subsets were developed to guarantee balanced representation from the data. The carefully calibrated MobileNetV3 model for enhanced generalization consisted in extra thick layers, dropout regularization, and categorical cross-entropy loss. Regarding specific foods like those that Ayam_pop and Dendeng_batokok ranked highly recall, the results revealed an outstanding general accuracy of 90%. Still, outwardly identical things like gulai_ikan and gulai_tunjang brought attention to areas needing repairs and generated classification issues. The efficiency of MobileNetV3 for culinary classification as well as its opportunities to help technical innovation and cultural preservation is underlined in this paper. The results open the path for scalable food recognition systems able of including many cuisines, thereby improving uses in the food sector, health monitoring, and beyond.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Early Detection of Cardiac Diseases: RNN Analysis of PTB XL+ Data
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Predicting cardiac conditions is vital for early intervention and personalized care. This study explores RNN models, including LSTM and GRU, for cardiac anomaly prediction using the PTB XL+ dataset, containing 21,837 12-lead ECG recordings. The dataset, covering myocardial infarction, arrhythmias, and conduction abnormalities, enables effective training and testing of predictive models. Dataset preprocessing, standardization, and augmentation improve the generalization and robustness of the model. The research shows the revolutionary ability of deep learning in medical diagnostics, particularly with cardiac conditions using ECG data to detect and predict. RNNs will thus be able to provide early diagnosis and targeted interventions that lead to better patient outcomes. Future work would then be concentrated on optimizing model architecture, further development of advanced variants of RNN, and fine-tuning hyperparameters to improve accuracy and robustness. This research work brings out the role deep learning can play in clinical practice for enhancement and promotion of preventive care. It explains the technique behind the model's decision-making process and factors predicted for performance. This work shows how the RNN model can be used to predict heart illness using ECG data which can, in turn, be implemented in clinical practice for early diagnosis and intervention. The accuracy by the RNN model achieved here is 74.6%.

articleTitle: Diabetic Foot Ulcer Diagnosis using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Diabetic Foot Ulcers (DFUs) are a serious diabetes complication, which mostly results in infection, amputation, and increased mortality if not addressed timely. Proper classification of DFUs is critical for early treatment and improved clinical outcomes. In the context of DFU image classification, this study compares the effectiveness of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with traditional Machine Learning (ML) models Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN). The CNN model is shown to outperform other models with much higher accuracy since it can extract pertinent features automatically from the images, while ML models depend on manually designed features and have comparatively poorer performance. The research also points to some major gaps in DFU classification, such as excessive intra-class variability, small dataset size, and class imbalance. The results have real-world applicability in the healthcare field by yielding AI-based DFU classification for timely diagnosis and intervention. Future work can build on improving model performance by increasing the dataset size, using transfer learning, and real-time deployment in clinics. The proposed model achieved 90.5% accuracy, 87.2% precision, 85.8% recall, and an F1-score of 86.78%.

articleTitle: BERT based Deep Learning Approach for Classification of Mental Health Disorders
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The rise of deep learning models for classification of mental disorders proven promising results. The transformer based CNN models like BERT is fairly accurate in processing neuro images, EEG signals, social media texts, clinical records and patient reviews from cancer treatment sites. This paper presents BERT based model trained with mental health data taken from Kaggle containing around 35k responses and 19 mental features. The major findings of this research highlights the accurate classification of mental states over traditional diagnostic methods. The train and test losses are collected for 100 epochs for the two BERT baselines. The strong correlation between the features relating to optimism & diagnosed-mapped (0.57) and concentration feature with sexual activity (0.63) shows that individuals with mental disorders tend to overthink more than the normal persons. The proposed model achieves 89% accuracy in classifying mental health in terms of bipolar disorders type I, II and depression.

articleTitle: Leveraging Neuromorphic Computing for Efficient and Scalable Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Neuromorphic computing is a new data analytical paradigm that mimics the behavior of biological neural systems to offer better computational power. State-of-the-art performance in conventional deep learning models (CNNs and transformers) comes at the expense of exorbitant energy and computation time. The real-time processing, low latency, and better energy efficiency make neuromorphic architectures to be a more appealing solution to kiosks where inferences on a large scale of data are being performed. In this paper, we discuss neuromorphic computing, how it can minimize data processing, its superiority compared to traditional AI models, and its future selection for diverse applications. Neuromorphic systems demonstrate a scalable way to the next-generation artificial intelligence by taking advantage of event-driven processing and dedicated hardware

articleTitle: AI Techniques in Leveraging Resume Screening System
