publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: A revolutionary era for resume development and screening is launched by the incorporation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Human Resources Management (HRM). It can be challenging to find and organize competent candidates for a post, especially if there are many applications. Because the ideal applicant becomes more difficult to find quickly, this can affect the development of the team. In this article, LSTM, a deep learning (DL) algorithm, and many machine learning (ML) algorithms, such as Kneighbors classifies, SVM, random forest, random forest, naive bays, logistic regulation and XGBOOST to compare and analyze using similar dataset. With a production of 83%, this model gets the best validity with LSTM approach and maximum accuracy with XG Boost. Increased recruitment satisfaction and productivity can lead to results from recruitment using the proposed structure to filter applicants who are more favorable for job criteria.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of YOLOv5 and YOLOv8 for Helmet Detection Inside ATMs
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Automated helmet detection inside automated teller machine (ATM) cabin for cash dispense can enhance security as well as serves as a means to prevent heist and vandalism. This study presents a comparative study on helmet detection inside ATMs using two prominent object detection you look only once (YOLO) v5 and YOLOv8. The system facilitates detection of helmets from closed circuit television (CCTV) footages to help in identifying the people entering into the ATM by wearing helmets and also in avoiding potential intrusion. In addition to precision and recall, mean average precision (mAP), a standard object detection metric to measure the accuracy of localization is used in this paper to assess the performance of helmet detection models constructed using YOLOv5 and YOLOv8. Experimental evaluation carried out in this study elucidates that YOLOv8 performs better than YOLOv5. By integrating the proposed model with IoT techniques, this model improves the safety and security. In addition, the incorporation of other alert models with this system offers a safer environment for the users inside the ATM cabin.

articleTitle: A Systematic Review of Deep Learning Techniques in Colon Cancer Screening
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Deep Learning is nowadays one of the powerful approaches of the Artificial Intelligence field in object detection and recognition. It also has gained reputation for improvement in the analysis of medical images. Early diagnosis and accuracy in prediction can be obtained by finding various normal and abnormal patterns in complex datasets by using different deep learning algorithms. Once deep learning models have undergone extensive training on enormous datasets, it can learn distinguishing between tissues that are either cancerous or not. Moreover, it improves precision in diagnosis and also enables better results in the outcomes of patients. This paper elaborates various deep learning architectures employed in investigating the state of the colon in diagnosing cancer. Deep learning algorithms which detect colon cancer help to identify various significant performance parameters to measure their effectiveness. The metrics include accuracy which helps to make the correct predictions, sensitivity metric to correctly identify the patients suffering from the disease and specificity metric to identify the people without the disease accurately. This paper will present reviews of different research papers that outline the overall framework. This paper will be beneficial for those researchers who are keen to know about different deep learning techniques for diagnosing the cancer in colon.

articleTitle: Hybrid AI Models for QoS Estimation in α-η-μ Fading and Co-Channel Interference Environments within 6G Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid AI model for QoS estimation in 6G networks by mitigating the challenges caused due to α-η-μ fading and co-channel interference. These incorporate a variety of machine learning strategies that deliver improved accuracy with respect to forecasting and real-time updating capabilities. We evaluate it using an extensive set of simulations, including heatmaps and time series analysis; we show substantial reductions on system throughput, latency and utilization. This model makes the design highly dynamic to accommodate a wide spectrum of network conditions and thereby optimizes resources utilization in the overall performance. The comparison proves the high performance of hybrid AI model compared to conventional and state-of-the-art techniques, making it a promising resolution for QoS estimation in advanced network environments.

articleTitle: Skin Lesion Classification Using Deep Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Classifying skin lesions, particularly melanoma, remains a significant challenge due to low contrast, high noise, and visual similarities among lesions. This research proposes an ensemble model combining Inception V3, DenseNet201, and EfficientNet B7, leveraging their unique strengths in capturing complex features from dermatoscopic images. By employing transfer learning with pre-trained models and fine-tuning on a melanoma dataset, the ensemble achieves remarkable accuracy, surpassing previous benchmarks. Specifically, the models attain accuracy rates of 89.9% (InceptionV3), 92.2% (DenseNet201), and 91.2% (EfficientNet B7). This study represents a critical step toward developing robust and efficient computer-aided melanoma classification systems for clinical use, though further clinical validation is needed.

articleTitle: Swarm based Computational Intelligence Techniques for Performance Optimization in Wireless Sensor and Actuator Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: WSANs are networks that are made of several distinct nodes that collectively understand the environment, subsequently change the state of the atmosphere, and select an appropriate action to perform after substituting on it. As a natural progression of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), WSANs present many of the same research difficulties as well as many new ones. These difficulties come from dealing with incomplete and complex optimization problems, ambiguous data, or processing and gathering data from different areas. Computational intelligence (CI) is a general term that refers to a group of naturally occurring and language-inspired methods that offer powerful answers to real-world problems. As a result, various investigators have moved to CI in their hopes of discovering results for several WSAN-related problems. The present paper examines the application of numerous CI approaches to the WSAN field and review the swarm-based CI techniques for performance optimization of WSANs. After reviewing and classifying previous works, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to maximize energy efficiency, load balancing, and fault tolerance in Wireless Sensor and Actuator Networks (WSANs) is implemented. A comparison of PSO, GA, and ACO in WSAN optimization problems shows that PSO consistently outperforms GA and ACO across all examined measures.

articleTitle: Instance Segmentation of Chest X-Ray Images Using Mask RCNN for Automated Pulmonary Tuberculosis Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: One of the most dangerous infectious respiratory diseases that affect people is tuberculosis (TB). It is essential to detect TB disease in the early stage; otherwise, it can lead to a life-threatening problem. This study proposed an automatic TB detection method based on deep learning, in which automatic analysis and classification of Chest X-Ray images (CXR) for Tb or not Tb was performed. With the Transfer Learning method for automated TB detection that reduces the cost and time, a deep learning-based approach called Mask RCNN is used for semantic interpretation of images. It is a state-of-the-art model trained to determine pixel level/instance segmentation for each object in the image used for TB detection with generalized feature extraction. ResNet 50 and ResNet 101 models were used for the experimental results and to compare the classification performance with DenseNet and Inception models. The experimental results indicate that Resnet 101 produces the best result with a Mean Average Precision of 94.33, and ResNet-50 produces 89 with a learning rate of 0.001.

articleTitle: Detection Of Counterfeit Images Through Deep Learning based Yolov3 Model
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Image forgery is the procedure of analysing and detecting any fraudulent or unauthorised alterations made to digital images. The detection in images is difficult for achieving a high accuracy rate and the process is time-consuming. Researchers and forensic experts are developing tools for detecting fake images. The identification of computer-generated picture forgeries is a notable area of study, aiming to provide a comprehensive review of detection tools and techniques. In this work, a novel deep-learning model is proposed for detecting forgery in images. The images are pre-processed using an adaptive Gaussian bilateral (AGB) filter to enhance the quality of the images. The enhanced photos are fed into the Mobile Net for extracting the relevant features in the pictures. The modified Yolov3 is utilized for object detection in images and detecting the real and forgery images. According to the result, the proposed model attains 99.55% for forgery detection in images. The modified Yolov3 yields 99.55% accuracy as opposed to Mask RCNN, RCNN, and SSD's 0.68%, 0.65%, and 1.16% accuracy. CNN, ResNetV2 and DCNN are all outperformed the proposed model in terms of overall accuracy by 0.11%, 1.10%, and 5.55%, respectively.

articleTitle: High Capacity and Secure Temporal Audio Steganography Model with Robustness Against Amplification
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Temporal domain audio steganography methods have clear benefits of being simple and computationally quick. However, the existing temporal domain methods that have high capacity, like the least significant bit (LSB) method, are highly sensitive to amplification attacks, which are very easy to implement. Amplification can completely destroy the hidden message even at undetectable levels such that discerning an attack from unintentional damage is hard. On the other hand the temporal domain algorithms that are actually robust against amplification have very low hiding capacity. A new method of temporal audio steganography is proposed here which is robust against amplification attacks while having high capacity, security and perceptual transparency. It builds on the basic difference expansion paradigm and applies cryptographic principles for enhanced security. The algorithm takes a stereo WAV cover file and secret message file, compresses and encrypts the secret file, and employs a transform domain algorithm to embed the resulting data into the cover WAV file. By exploiting properties of stereo WAV files, the algorithm succeeds in being more robust toward attacks of amplification. Performance analysis is done using peak signal to noise ratio (PSNR), signal to noise ratio (SNR), mean square error (MSE) and Hamming distance.

articleTitle: Outlier Detection in High-Dimensional Data using t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: In this study, the focus is to use the t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) technique for identifying outliers from high dimensional data sets. To this end, the study proposes to use t-SNE with other clustering algorithms with the view of improving upon the performance of outlier detection. The percentage prognostications were based on the results obtained by applying the proposed methodology on three sets: CIFAR-10, KDD Cup 1999, and HAR; the last one yielded an accuracy of 89%. 5%, 92. 3%, and 93. With K-Means clustering, it was possible to make predictions of the number of patients for the next year with a 95% accuracy while the patients’ age was clustered into two groups with an 8% error and gender into two groups with an 8% error. The findings show that widely acclaimed t-SNE can be used to identify clusters and anomalies in large datasets. In future works additional, efforts will be made to determine optimal values of t-SNE parameters and, also, to investigate the possibilities of further combining of t-SNE with various machine learning models.

articleTitle: Impact of Handcrafted Features and Raw Image Data on Neural Network Performance: Insights from the Brodatz Texture Database
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Key computer vision tasks include image retrieval and classification, which are used extensively in fields including multimedia, security, and healthcare. This study contrasts conventional deep learning methods combined with feature extraction techniques.The study extracts feature by combining Completed Local Binary Patterns (CSLBP) and Grey Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM), which are then put into a Dense Neural Network (DNN). CSLBP captures local texture patterns with reduced complexity, while GLCM analyzes the spatial relationships and co-occurrence of pixel intensities, enabling a robust representation of image features. Convolutional neural networks, or CNNs, are used in parallel for direct image classification. In comparison to the CNN model, which achieved data accuracy of 69.46%, the DNN with handcrafted features produced a test accuracy of 75.71% along with improved recall, precision, and F1-score values, according to the evaluation of both models. Plots of accuracy and loss throughout training and validation are also included in the study to show how the two models converge. These findings indicate that a DNN using handcrafted features performs better than a CNN and highlights the efficacy of conventional feature extraction techniques in image classification applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Online Retail Insights: K-Means Clustering and PCA for Customer Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Businesses seeking to enhance online retail operations and gain a deeper understanding of consumer behavior must effectively segment their clientele. This study introduces a comprehensive approach that integrates K-Means clustering for customer segmentation with Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction. Using this approach on a large online retail dataset using Recency, Frequency, and Monetary (RFM) metrics greatly reduces data complexity while preserving important variances. This approach helps to identify individual client categories, so improving focused marketing plans and streamlining retail industry decision-making. This method facilitates the identification of different client segments, hence enhancing focused marketing strategies and improving decision-making in the retail sector. The framework serves as an excellent instrument for data-driven customer relationship management, exhibiting both scalability and interpretability. This study addresses critical limitations, including dependence on transactional data and a unique dataset, as well as future directions that involve the integration of supplementary data sources, investigation of advanced clustering methodologies, and enablement of real-time implementation. The results highlight the effectiveness of combining PCA and K-Means to improve customer segmentation in dynamic retail settings.

articleTitle: PMSChain: A Blockchain-based Prison Management System using the Ethereum Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The prison system in India lags other industries, such as healthcare, in terms of automation. The existing prison management system often lacks transparency, consistency in security information, and well-defined procedures. To address this issue, we developed a system to digitize daily prison operations. The proposed blockchain-based prison management system is a comprehensive software application designed to manage activities related to prisons using a distributed ledger for efficient storage and managing information related to lawbreakers. The prison authority can have access to add, delete, or update the lawbreaker data that is collected from the police. The suggested system defines various roles for accessing the data inside the prison. Proper and timely access to data is enabled for the prison authorities. The proposed system has been implemented using the Ethereum Sepolia test net with 1000 tractions and its total transaction cost is 0.015357. Additionally, gas price, throughput, and latency has been computed for the proposed work. This system has been designed to provide secure, efficient, and user-friendly management of inmate records, scheduling, and communication. This system enables tamper-proofness, accountability and security of data by incorporating blockchain technology for secure and immutable record transaction within prison which prevents fraud, and corruption.

articleTitle: Lead-Uwsn: Adaptive Hybrid Lion Dolphin Algorithm for Dynamic Packet Delivery in UWSN
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Underwater wireless sensor networks (UWSN) are viewed as promising technologies to gather meaningful data from underwater areas, especially to support environmental forecasting and military functions. The challenges presented in UWSNs with respect to the reliability and efficiency of underwater sensor nodes are a major concern for packet delivery in the network path. To address these issues, a new LEAD-UWSN technique is proposed in this work. The proposed LEAD-UWSN hybridizes the Lion Optimization Algorithm (LOA) and Dolphin Echolocation Algorithm (DEA) to reduce the issues encountered in underwater settings, such as packet losses, power consumption, and network delays. The proposed work LEAD-UWSN also improves the accuracy and efficiency of packet transmission over UWSN by integrating these LOA and DEA algorithms. The proposed technique was tested using MATLAB. The performance of LEAD-UWSN was evaluated in terms of end-to-end delay, packet delivery, energy consumption, and throughput. The results show that the proposed method has high efficiency and high reliability in comparison with performance metrics. The proposed method achieves a 6.59% accuracy in packet delivery with respect to transmission.

articleTitle: Strengthening Water Utility Cybersecurity: Evaluating Detection Algorithms with BATADAL
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: With increased levels of digitalization and networked systems, maintaining the security of water utilities has gained prime importance. Digital infrastructure has tremendously improved operational efficiency for the water system but exposed its critical systems to various cyber threats. The cybersecurity of water utilities would alleviate the risks of water supply contamination, service disruption, and economic consequences. Detection algorithm evaluation is thus a crucial step in strengthening security measurements. The Battle of the Attack Detection Algorithms BATADAL gives an exclusive opportunity to rigorously test the strength of several detection algorithms designed to apply to water systems. Realistic cyber-attacks simulated through BATADAL will go a long way in rigorous testing and evaluation so researchers and practitioners can pinpoint the most potent detection strategies. A comparative evaluation for the precision of Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Decision Tree (DT) shows that SVM is superior to RF and DT because of its robustness in dealing with high-dimensional data. Precision is high since the decision boundary is optimized for SVM, so the best performance is in SVM among the three, and the observed accuracy is 97.09. This enhances the water infrastructure's ability and safeguards vital resources while ensuring the community's safe water supply is not interrupted.

articleTitle: An Artificial Intelligence-based Sign Language Recognition using Attention-Enhanced Long Short-Term Memory Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Sign language recognition is essential for enabling communication between the deaf-mute community and the broader population, helping to bridge significant communication barriers. Current techniques tend to use expensive sensors or custom hardware, but this research provides a low cost, AI approach to sign language recognition using video input. An AI model has been proposed in this work that utilizes a self-curated dataset of 14 essential gestures, designed to capture a wide range of commonly used expressions, and employs an LSTM network enhanced with an attention mechanism to capture temporal dependencies. This method allows the model to concentrate on the key frames in the gesture sequences, and can recognize much better, without having to have a lot of processing power. The proposed model achieved an accuracy of 92.1% across 14 gesture classes, demonstrating the feasibility of an efficient and accessible sign language recognition system. This work provides a foundational step toward accessible communication tools for the deaf-mute community, encouraging broader adoption through mobile and low-cost devices.

articleTitle: Enhanced Graph Convolutional Networks with Adaptive Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Graph neural networks represent the latest promising advances in deep learning models to analyze graph-structured data, but traditional models, such as the Graph Convolutional Network, have scalability issues such as oversmoothing and lack of generalization. This work extends the standard GCN by proposing adaptive aggregation functions, scalable normalization techniques, and robust regularization methods. The proposed change dynamically selects aggregation strategies based on graph properties, improves the computational efficiency at optimality, and enhances the model generalization, especially on large complex graphs. The improved GCN was tested in relation to the major metrics: accuracy, cross-entropy loss, and F1 score. Experimental results show a 6.5% increase in accuracy and a 20% reduction in runtime compared with baselines like GAT and GraphSAGE. This makes the model more apt for real-time applications and scalable datasets. However, the approach brought out the shortcomings of handling highly dynamic, sparse graphs. Future developments would include joint integration of attention mechanisms with recurrent neural networks, hybrid architectures that capture dynamic graph structures, and better fitting into evolving topologies.

articleTitle: Improving Accuracy in Market Close Prediction Using Optimized Financial Indicators
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The stock market is a dynamic and complex financial system where buyers and sellers trade shares of publicly listed companies. Predicting next-day stock prices involves understanding the interplay of multiple factors that influence price movements. This study employs various machine learning algorithms to predict next-day stock prices using a comprehensive set of features, including 27 indicator values, along with metrics such as open, close, high, low, volume, and the overall market index value. A total of 17 machine learning algorithms and nine feature selection techniques were utilized, with models evaluated using RMSE, MAE, and MAPE. Unlike previous studies, which often focus on price prediction using limited combinations of features and algorithms, this research adopts a novel approach by integrating these diverse elements. Additionally, the motor sector, an underexplored area in stock price prediction, was analyzed. Among the models tested, Ridge regression with forward feature selection demonstrated the best performance, achieving a MAE of 0.881. This study lays the groundwork for future research by extending the scope to other sectors and exploring advanced machine learning and deep learning models combined with feature selection techniques.

articleTitle: Predicting Student Success in Online Learning Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: With the quick expansion of online education, understanding user engagement and performance metrics has become crucial for improving learning outcomes. This study analyzes a dataset which encompasses comprehensive details about user demographics, engagement levels and course performance in online learning environments using machine learning. The motivation behind this work is to uncover factors influencing course completion rates, engagement patterns and overall learning success by exploring eleven different ML models along with the comparison of three data balancing/sampling and six feature selection techniques. The best of the four data balancing techniques, TOMEK Links and the best of the six feature selection techniques, Chi-square test are preferred based on the model performances examined using evaluation metrics and the time taken by the models. Out of all the models, the five best performing models are LightGBM, XGBoost, Decision Tree (entropy), KNN and ADA Boost. Finally, the explainable AI tools LIME and SHAP are used for model interpretation. Decision Tree with accuracy 1 and highest macro F1 score 0.97 became the best model which executed within 0.37 seconds being the least time.

articleTitle: Leveraging Attention Mechanisms in ResNet101 for Enhanced Facial Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Facial emotion recognition serves many real-world applications across health care and security and human-computer interaction because these fields require advanced models recognizing emotions under true practical situations. The proposed Advanced Facial Emotion Recognition (FER) system utilizes ResNet-101 with Attention Mechanism to resolve gaps found in conventional methods whose examples include: ResNet50 and DeepExpr together with Ensemble Multi-feature approaches and both Adversarial neural networks and Attentional CNNs. The proposed framework demonstrate limited capability to recognize fine-grained embodied perceptions including emotions as well as faces and views together with novel realistic environmental changes and obscuring effects. The proposed model detects five complex emotions (sadness, anger, happiness, disgust and neutrality) by giving specific attention to the targeted emotion regions in facial areas. The proposed system reports F1 scores between 0.92 to 0.95 alongside evaluations demonstrating precision ranging from 0.88 to 0.97 and recall ranging from 0.92 to 0.95 for all emotions. This method demonstrates 99.6% accuracy in recognition yet its Kappa score stands at 94.1 because of slight discrepancies compared to classic models.

articleTitle: NovaNet-SSL: A Self-Supervised DDPM Model for Underwater Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Marine images suffer from severe tint of color and blurry feature caused by distortion in water. Enhancement of such images is necessary to be developed for the improvement of quality vision tasks underwater. This paper proposes a self-supervised diffusion model, called NovaNet, for real-time enhancement of underwater images (UIE). This technique uses the power of DDPM and optimized the process using self-supervised learning. NovaNet accelerates the inference process without a compromise on enhancement quality; it performs faster and more accurately than any other generative model. Unlike conventional DDPM models, which suffer from slow processing and color bias while used for UIE, this approach integrates self-supervised learning to effectively guide the model, improving the quality of image restoration. The novelty in this approach is self-supervised learning with diffusion-based image restoration to produce results of high quality, that is, enhanced quality output and fast processing speed. NovaNet demonstrates a 20.34% improvement in PSNR, a 0.5351% gain in SSIM, and achieves a 0.036% faster processing speed compared to existing models. This proposed model is tested against several challenging real-world underwater datasets, which are characterized to have superior performance regarding enhanced quality and real-time process capabilities.

articleTitle: Automated Malaria Detection Using Deep Learning and the Lacuna Dataset
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Malaria is one of the primary health issues in resource-poor environments, and treatment for it is very time-sensitive and requires high accuracy in diagnosis. Toward this end, this paper relies on the Lacuna Malaria Detection Dataset of microscopic blood smear images annotated for the presence of malaria parasites to develop a convolutional neural network-based automatic malaria parasite detection framework. The dataset is a collection of thick and thin blood smear images, thus enabling the development of highly predictive models. It makes use of state-of-the-art techniques in image preprocessing, optimized CNN architectures, and rigorous evaluation metrics to ensure that the model developed will attain a high degree of accuracy and generalizability. The developed model yielded approximately 98% accuracy in detection and may potentially be useful for the accurate identification of the parasites. This study has placed a lot of attention on the practical application of AI diagnostic tools within health care, especially toward the under-resourced regions.

articleTitle: Data Analytics for Identifying and Reducing Hospital Readmissions
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Data analytics examines healthcare data to identify patterns and personalize care plans ultimately by reducing hospital readmissions. Readmissions after discharge increase healthcare costs, lower quality, and dissatisfied patients. To overcome these issues, a novel Data analytics approach has been proposed to reduce hospital readmissions. This inquiry begins with a complete dataset of clinical data, patient demographics, and Electronic Health Records (EHRs). Initially, the data gathered from the clinical data, patient demographics, and electronic health records are fed to the preprocessing module for transforming raw healthcare data into a structured form for analysis. After preprocessing, an Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) is performed which simplifies the initial insights and hospital readmission risk factor identification. The most essential features are selected from the analyzed outcomes of EDA for readmission prediction. After feature selection, the development of hospital readmission models uses three data analytics methods. At first, the Machine Learning (ML) based methods predict the readmission status and the sequential relationships and anticipate readmission risk over time are captured using a neural network. Finally, the patient groups with comparable readmission trends are identified through hierarchical clustering. After data analytics, those outcomes are fed to the real-time patient monitoring system to reveal readmission factors such as discharge planning and timely drug management. The proposed method is validated by using healthcare datasets. In comparison, the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 97% whereas, the predictive modeling, risk factor, care process, and alert method achieves 85%, 78%, 90%, and 83% respectively.

articleTitle: Inclusive and Intelligent Traffic Management System for the Physically Impaired Pedestrians
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: This study investigates the consideration of physically impaired pedestrians in the existing traffic management system. Although IoT-driven intelligent systems have shown promise in managing traffic flow and incident detection, they overlook the specific needs of physically impaired individuals, leading to longer waiting times and safety. First, an Inclusive and Intelligent Traffic Management System (IITMS) is proposed, designed to support the independent mobility of physically impaired pedestrians by dynamically adjusting traffic signals and incorporating Vehicle to Everything (V2X). The framework integrates CCTV cameras with the YOLOv9 model for detecting individuals with mobility aids including crutches, wheelchairs, and walking frames, at pedestrian crossings. Integrated with V2X for communication amongst vehicles and pedestrians, an action selection strategy algorithm for enhanced optimization of real-time processing by maintaining optimal traffic flow for all users to enhance operational efficiency is then introduced. The simulation results show that integrating IITMS, V2X and an action selection strategy algorithm achieves 94% detection accuracy across various physical impairment categories and enhances operational efficiency compared to non-optimized models.

articleTitle: Artificial Rabbit Combined K-medoid Golden Eagle Optimization for Energy Efficient Routing in WSN
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Energy harvesting (EH) in Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) collects ambient energy to power sensor nodes which reduces battery reliance and extends the network lifetime (NL). However, drawbacks include variability in energy sources, conversion inefficiencies, and energy distribution imbalances, that impact network stability. To overcome these issues a novel artificial Rabbit Optimization-based Adaptive K-Medoid golden eagle for WSN (ROAM-WSN) is proposed for reducing the reliance on conventional power sources and extending the network's operational lifetime. Initially, the system utilises a hybrid energy harvesting system to gather energy from diverse natural and artificial sources to ensure consistent energy availability for sensor nodes in the network. The harvested energies are converted into usable electrical energy through an energy conversion mechanism and stored in the energy storage units. After energy conversion, a hybrid clustering-based optimisation selects optimal Cluster Heads (CHs) to minimise energy consumption (EC). Finally, an artificial optimization algorithm enhances the CH selection for reliable transmission through routing. The ROAM-WSN framework is simulated by using a network simulator (NS3). In comparison, the proposed ROAM-WSN approach achieves a low energy consumption of 20J, then EHRWO of 37J, LCEHA of 42, and LANTERN of 33J respectively.

articleTitle: A New Era of Malaria’s Disease Control using AI-Driven Predictive Models
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Malaria remains a public health menace affecting around more than 240 million cases, and hundreds of thousands of deaths per annum with most cases reported from Sub-Saharan region. Advancement in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning offers transformative solutions in malarial control using predictive analytics, programmed diagnostics, effective treatment and malarial drug discovery. This paper aims to explore the use of AI in managing malaria, outlining methodologies like Recurrent Neural Networks that can predict malarial outbreaks with high efficiency, Convolutional Neural Networks for blood smears detection and Deep Learning models for identifying new drug combinations for malarial management. AI can be useful in vector control by reviewing the behavior and environment of mosquitoes to improve the efficiency of the treatments and its implementation in malaria diagnosis and tailored treatment decreasing human error and smoothening the use of resources while speeding up the treatment process. The long-term advancement includes both AI technology in geo-spatial and predictive analytics in real-time approach to epidemic surveillance and management of resources. Genetic markers for patients and individual treatment history shall also continue to expand the possibilities of the management of malaria. However, issues like ethical hurdles, collection and protection of patient data and medical implementation need to be attended. It is therefore important to engage collective efforts of governments, non-government organizations as well as technology delivering firms to unlock the full potential of AI in eliminating malaria and in improving global health outcomes worldwide.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Driven Surrogate Modeling and Quantum Metaheuristics for Gurney Flap Optimization in Darrieus Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The optimization of Darrieus wind turbine designs is critical to improving their aerodynamic performance and energy efficiency. The present study focuses to enhance the (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</inf> ) of the turbine by optimizing the design parameters of Gurney flaps attached to the trailing edges of the turbine rotors. Specifically, the flap angle and height are treated as the design variables. To explore the design space and generate random design points efficiently, Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) is employed. URANS simulations are carried out on these design points to provide high-fidelity data. A RBF surrogate model is then trained on this data, and is integrated with the Quantum-based Salp Swarm Algorithm (QSSA). The findings indicate a significant improvement in C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</inf> , with the optimized Gurney flap configurations outperforming the smooth baseline case by approximately 158% and the initial Gurney flap setup by 188%. Further, the performance of QSSA is shown with another popular evolutionary algorithm— the Harris Hawks Algorithm. This approach demonstrates the potential of data-driven optimization techniques in the energy sector.

articleTitle: Smart Farming: CNN-Based Rice Variety Classification for Global Impact
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The cultured variety is Oryza sativa and it is consumed daily by over 50% of the global populace, with differences between the rice varieties made on grain size, aroma, texture and ease of cooking. Some of the famous types include Karacadag, Basmati, Jasmine, Arborio, and Ipsala. The processes used previously in rice classification involved visual methods and were tedious, inconclusive, and imprecise. As the world continues to produce more rice, there is a strong need to employ innovative classification techniques that can serve the purpose as needed. The current research introduces a deep learning algorithm called Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) as a useful tool for rice variety classification. CNNs perform exceptionally well when training images for classification where features from images are learned to determine different patterns, which include but are not limited to texture and shape. The CNN model training involves use of dataset of 80,000 images of five rice variety images with each image resized to 256 x 256 pixels. To improve the classification accuracy and avoid overfitting, the authors use four approaches including data augmentation and convolutional and pooling layers. The outcomes of the proposed model show a high prediction accuracy level, 98%, which proves that CNNs can be applied to rice sorting and grading automation. This presents the findings of this study alongside a unique solution all farmers could apply to improve rice quality control and marketability, which in turn offer cheaper ways of improving its quality hence benefiting the global rice industry.

articleTitle: Blockchain Meets AI: Future of Decentralized Digital Commerce with ONDC
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Blockchain combined with Artificial Intelligence within the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) executes a transformation of decentralized digital commerce operations through systems improving both security capabilities and transparency while boosting performance rates and user experience quality. The combination of Blockchain and Artificial Intelligence provides secure transaction automation using smart contracts with longtime data protection plus tailored vendor matching along with fraud prevention and instant customer service capabilities. The research unites predictive analytical capabilities from Artificial Intelligence with decentralized blockchain identity validation systems to enhance operational trust and efficiency. The resulting system provides enhanced transaction security with reduced fraud and automated payments based on smart contracts as well as simplified returns procedures and peak vendor visibility which drives improved customer satisfaction in a more competitive market. AI and Blockchain together at ONDC establish a secure marketplace which delivers efficient customer-driven digital commerce while fundamentally reshaping online shopping operations.

articleTitle: Infrared Eye Image Classification: A Deep Learning Approach for Enhanced Eye State Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Applications, ranging from detection of fatigue to glance tracking for medical diagnosis, are highly reliant on accurate classification of states, open or closed. This work creates a more robust and efficient classifier based on deep learning using a complete set of IR eye images in the MRL Eye Dataset. Under different lighting conditions and varied modifications in devices, the architecture CNN was used to train the model in detecting eye states. Through much testing and optimization, the model achieved brilliant validation accuracy of 98%, which probably deepened its ability to generalize in different test settings. Techniques used to improve the performance and reduce overfitting include data augmentation, dropout regularization, and fine-tuning. The approach proposed here provides a scalable solution for many real-world applications requiring high levels of dependability and accuracy and really underscores the value of IR imaging for classifications of conditions in the eye. This work emphasizes the scope of possibilities whereby one might push the boundaries of eye state recognition systems by the incorporation of such domain-specific datasets with advanced deep learning methods.

articleTitle: Deep Vein Thrombosis Segmentation via Deep Learning based U-Net using MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a prevalent medical condition. For pulmonary embolism to prevent potentially fatal acute consequences, an accurate identification of deep vein thrombosis is essential. In this paper, a novel VT-Seg has been proposed to segment the DVT using MRI images. Initially, the input MRI images are pre-processed using Multi-Scale Retinex (MSR) for enhancing the image. The enhanced images are classified using MobileNet to identify normal and deep vein thrombosis. The next phase uses U-Net to segment the deep vein thrombosis cases. Efficacy is determined by analysing F-measure, specificity, accuracy, Jaccard index, and Dice coefficient enhancement. Compared to the U-Net, traditional networks like Grabcut, Otsu method, and SegNet obtain less accuracy. The accuracy ranges of 99.25% are preserved with U-Net. According to the proposed VT-Seg approach, the overall efficiency of MSMT-DL, ResNet-101, and construct fusion models is improved by 3.15%, 26.35%, and 34.42%, respectively.

articleTitle: Cloud-Based Digital Twin for Cybersecurity Threat Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Cyber threats are evolving into the ever-skyscraper-oriented monster with increasing scope and complexity and demand for contemporary security models that focus on live threat detection and response. In this study, a Cloud-Based Digital Twin (CBDT) approach is proposed for predicting and mitigating cybersecurity threats by employing machine learning in the digital twin domain to bolster cyber resilience. The framework proposed becomes a virtualized cloud environment replicating the IT infrastructure of the organization and allowing simulation, detection, and prediction of cyber threats in real time. Through the integration of machine learning models like Random Forest, Convolutional neural networks (CNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), the CBDT framework enhances the processes of anomaly detection, threat classification, and incident response automation. LSTM has been shown to offer a best-in-class detection rate (96.1%) of a wide variety of cyber threats and consistently minimizes time to response vs. traditional intrusion detection systems. Furthermore, deployments in the cloud open new capabilities around scale, connecting vast threat intelligence data, and rapid analysis. Conclusively, the investigation highlights the promise of digital twins in cybersecurity, providing a proactive and adaptable defense strategy against the ever-changing landscape of cyber vulnerabilities.

articleTitle: Deep Transfer Learning Enabled Eye Gaze and Blink-Driven Support System for Paralysed Patients
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: This paper addresses the major communication and mobility challenges faced by paralysed patients mainly with Locked-in Syndrome (LIS) and Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), which makes the patient paralysed and causes speech disorders, and thus limiting their independence to talk and move freely. Traditional methods of controlling wheelchairs require appropriate position and lighting conditions. This research present a novel system that utilises eye-gaze detection to enable these patients to control a wheelchair, enhancing their ability to move wherever needed and communicate effectively. The approach employs advanced object detection techniques, specifically the YOLOv8 model, combined with gaze detection ability through an integrated Inception-ResNet-v2 architecture. This allows the entire system to accurately identify gaze directions (straight, left, right, closed (for reverse)) and YOLOv8 identifies the eye states (open or closed) compared to the conventional tracking methods, which fail under poor lighting conditions and precise positioning constraints. The developed model has attained an accuracy of 86.3% in detecting open and closed eyes, and an accuracy of 90.2% in eye gaze tracking, enabling effective communication through blink detection and mobility control through gaze. This innovative solution aims to improve the quality of life for paralyzed patients by providing them with a reliable means of mobility and communication, empowering them to engage more fully with their surroundings.

articleTitle: Optimizing Astronomical Image Classification with EfficientNetB0: A Comprehensive Study of Celestial Object Identification
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Advancing the knowledge of the universe, helping to discover and identify celestial bodies, and enabling study in astrophysics and cosmology depend on astronomical picture classification, which also supports Cataloging large volumes of data produced by telescopes depends on proper classification of astronomical images, which also helps astronomers to effectively spot trends and anomalies that can lead to new discoveries, therefore supporting sustainable innovation. In this work we categorize a hierarchically structured astronomical image dataset using EfficientNetB0, a deep learning model renowned for its accuracy and efficiency. There are 4,099 high-quality photos in the dataset; 3,279 for training and 820 for testing split. Using its capacity to scale both resolution and depth, the model was modified to execute macro- and fine-grained classification challenges. We obtained a classification accuracy of 89% following model training, therefore proving its efficiency in managing challenging astronomical data. This result emphasizes the possibilities of using modern convolutional neural networks for dependable and efficient classification in astronomical research, so supporting the development of automated systems for celestial object detection, which is absolutely vital for scientific advancement, quality education, and the encouragement of infrastructure development.

articleTitle: Advanced AI Technique and IoT Integration for Predicting and Preventing Flammable Gas and Toxic Vapor Leaks
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: This study’s ambition is to develop and integrate an advanced AI approach with IoT networks to quantitatively predict and prevent flammable gas and toxic vapor emissions. The main goal of such integration is to enhance safety and minimize the adverse effects on the surrounding environment. Ensuring high-quality, consistent data from various IoT sensors and integrating diverse data sources in real-time is challenging and crucial for AI model performance. Deploying AI models in real-world environments demands robust real-time processing, low latency, and high reliability, especially in dynamic industrial settings with potential connectivity and resource constraints. Deep Learning and XGBoost techniques will be utilized to address issues with data quality, integration, and real-time processing in the prediction and prevention of flammable gas and toxic vapor leaks, aiming to improve accuracy and operational efficiency. Leveraging Advanced AI techniques allows for proactive identification and timely alerting of potential gas leaks, thereby strengthening preemptive safety protocols. This technology supports ongoing monitoring and adaptive response functionalities, effectively reducing downtime and operational disturbances within industrial settings. The overall performance of the XGBoost classifier was 89%, precision 83%, Recall 100%, F1 score 91%. Time taken was 06 seconds, the neural network model achieved 94% accuracy, 91% precision, 100% recall and F1 score was 95%. As for the training time, this model took 5. 10 seconds.

articleTitle: ResNet18-Based Deep Learning Approach for Efficient and Accurate Nail Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Nail diseases are often overlooked in early stages, but timely detection is crucial for effective treatment and preventing further complications. This study presents an efficient and accurate deep learning approach using the ResNet18 architecture to detect various nail diseases. Leveraging the power of ResNet18, a lightweight yet robust convolutional neural network, we train our model to classify nail images into six categories: Acral Lentiginous Melanoma, Healthy Nail, Onychogryphosis, Blue Finger, Clubbing, and Pitting. To enhance model performance, we incorporate data augmentation techniques such as color jitter, random affine transformations, and horizontal and vertical flipping, enabling the model to learn complex and varied visual patterns associated with each condition. The ResNet18 model achieves a classification accuracy of over 91% on a validated dataset, with high precision, recall, and F1-scores across all classes, proving its ability to handle real-world variability in nail images. The approach addresses the computational challenges in medical image processing by utilizing an optimized ResNet18 model, which ensures quick inference suitable for clinical and remote applications. The confusion matrix analysis reveals the model’s strong performance, with minimal misclassifications between categories, even in visually similar cases. This research offers a scalable solution for nail disease detection, demonstrating the potential for deep learning to enhance dermatological diagnostics, particularly in resource-limited settings. By automating nail disease detection, this study contributes to improved accessibility and early intervention in nail health.

articleTitle: Advancements in Breast Cancer Detection: A Comprehensive Review of Deep Learning-Based Classification and Segmentation Techniques Using Ultrasound Imaging
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Breast cancer remains one of the most prevalent causes of mortality among women worldwide, underscoring the critical importance of early detection and accurate diagnosis. Ultrasound imaging has gained prominence due to its accessibility, cost-effectiveness, and safety, especially for younger women and those with dense breast tissue. However, inherent challenges such as low spatial resolution, speckle noise, and variability in image quality pose significant hurdles to precise analysis. Recent advancements in deep learning techniques have revolutionized breast cancer detection, particularly in the classification and segmentation of ultrasound images. This review analyzes state-of-the-art methods utilizing existing available datasets like BUSI, OASBUD, and KAIMRC. Classification models have demonstrated impressive performance, with Himel et al. achieving 99.7% accuracy, 99.71% F1-score, and an AUC of 99.9% using ensemble deep learning approaches. Similarly, segmentation models have achieved remarkable outcomes, with Hekal et al. reporting a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 92.92% and an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 87.39%. Integrated models combining classification and segmentation have further improved detection capabilities; for instance, Bobowicz et al. achieved 93.7% classification accuracy and an 87% DSC for segmentation. While these advancements are promising, challenges such as limited dataset diversity, variability in ultrasound imaging, and generalizability remain. Future research should explore hybrid models, transfer learning, and larger, multi-institutional datasets to enhance segmentation precision and classification reliability, paving the way for robust clinical applications.

articleTitle: Optimized Voice Activity Detection for Audio Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The advancement in virtual assistant tools has augmented the scope and development of the speech processing application. In any such application, speech signals undergo pre-processing stages such as noise cancellation and silence removal. This study aims to develop a method to reconstruct a given audio recordings by removing silences, in order to improve the quality of speech signal. In this article, a novel silence removal technique termed as Optimized Voice Activity for Audio Signal Processing (OVAD-ASP) is presented. This technique is observed to effectively remove the silences embedded in audio signals, with assured consistency, scalability and reliability. The is designed to use Standard Deviation for the silence removal. The proposed OVAD-ASP was developed using MATLAB. The proposed OVAD-ASP method has a salient feature of determining the threshold dynamically for silent removal. Therefore, the thresholds were selected and tested using random thresholds and statistical thresholds, specifically mean and standard deviation are considered to determine the dynamic threshold from the input audio files, of which standard deviation yielded more encouraging results than the conventional approaches, namely Zero Crossing Rate (ZCR), Short Time Energy (STE), and Root Mean Square Energy (RMSE). It is observed that the results of OVAD-ASP are encouraging, as endorsed by Average Mean Squared Error of 0.0046 and Average Similarity Ratio of 89.3%. Therefore, the OVAD-ASP plays a vital and inevitable role in speech preprocessing.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Networks for Enhanced Real-Time Traffic Incident Detection and Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Traffic incident detection and classification are essential aspects of enhancing road safety and efficiency. A new approach to enhancing real-time traffic incident detection and image classification with the help of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), viz., Alex Net, is presented in this paper. Alex Net, a deep CNN architecture that is widely used for image recognition, is employed to classify traffic images and videos for incident identification. The system makes use of the ability of the model to learn robust features to identify images as different events, such as accidents, roadblocks, and vehicle breakdowns. Low latency and high accuracy incident identification is done by the system utilizing real-time traffic camera data and Alex Net. Differentiation between different types of events. This is for the sake of enhancing reaction time, enabling effective traffic management, and differentiating between events. AlexNet enables 92% accuracy in real-time traffic detection and image classification, enhancing the efficiency of intelligent transportation systems. The results demonstrate how deep learning (DL) methods can revolutionise traffic monitoring systems and improve safety protocols for drivers.

articleTitle: Exploring Retinal Vessel Segmentation: Deep Learning Models and Their Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Retinal vascular segmentation is essential for the early identification and monitoring of numerous ocular and systemic conditions, including diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and hypertension. The emergence of deep learning methodologies, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and U-Net architectures, has markedly enhanced the precision and efficacy of retinal vascular segmentation. This review paper extensively examines contemporary deep learning methodologies, concentrating on model structures, problems, and assessment measures. This paper discusses the strengths of deep learning techniques in improving upon the limitations of traditional image processing methods, such as thresholding and edge detection, while handling complex vascular structures and varied image quality. It also emphasizes the availability of publicly accessible datasets, namely DRIVE, STARE, and CHASE_DB1, as research tools in this discipline. Despite this significant progress, a lot remains to be desired, including large-scale annotated datasets, computational demand, and problems in generalization across diverse populations. Finally, the paper concluded with some future directions by integrating explainable deep learning, multi-modal imaging, and the development of lightweight models that are more appropriate for real-time clinical use.

articleTitle: Lidar-Based Car Detection and Position Estimation Using Convolutional Neural Networks for Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Despite the many applications of computer vision in robotics, automation, and self-driving cars, object detection remains a significant difficulty. Recent developments in object recognition and image classification, in particular convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have significantly aided in the development of neural networks that enable practical applications in autonomous driving. This study uses a modified CNN architecture designed for accurate 3-D item identification to examine vehicle recognition and spatial analysis utilizing LiDAR data. The network offers robust localization even in difficult environments with occlusions using point-based bounding box predictions. Using a RANSAC-based refinement technique, the suggested system achieved a classification accuracy of 96.71% with bounding box precision significantly enhanced after 246 epochs of extensive evaluation on the KITTI dataset. These results validate the model's strong generalization ability in real-world scenarios with mirrored, noisy, and variable-oriented data. The findings validate the growing significance of CNNs in addressing autonomous navigation challenges. By contributing to the development of safer and more reliable transportation networks, our work ultimately moves the road toward completely autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Innovative Home Security Systems: A Comparative Analysis of IoT-Driven Solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: This study explores the evolution of home security and automation systems, driven by the growing need for safety and convenience in residential spaces. It analyzes various systems employing microcontroller technologies like Arduino Uno, ESP8266, and Raspberry Pi. These systems incorporate dual-password authentication, remote notifications via GSM modules, and IoT capabilities to monitor environmental factors such as motion, gas leaks, and temperature. By examining features like PIR sensors with cameras, RFID-based access control, and mobile applications for alerts, the study highlights innovative technological integrations in modern security solutions. While many systems showcase robust functionalities, concerns regarding false alarms and user discretion are significant. This study suggest the future advancements that could be included improved machine learning algorithms for enhanced intrusion detection, better device interoperability, and increased reliance on cloud-based solutions for data management. Overall, the research emphasizes the transformative role of IoT, GSM, and RFID technologies in home security.

articleTitle: Advanced Image Recognition for Mango Leaf Disease Diagnosis: A CNN-Based Study
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The abstract presents an all-rounded evaluation of the model crafted for classifying various mango leaf diseases, building its performance metrics, including precision, recall, F1-score, support, support proportion, and accuracy. Model Performance With a precision score of 97.32%, Red Rust was considered outstanding, with Black Tip garnering the second-highest at a precision score of 97.39%. Other diseases such as Sooty Mold, Leaf Gall, and Dieback displayed slightly lower precision values with 96.89%, 96.95%, and 96.91% respectively. With 10,380 photos in the dataset, the model's overall accuracy was a remarkable 97.10%. The recall values were also equally as impressive as the precision values, thus indicating a good model in terms of correctly identifying positives within each class as well since the F1-scores indicate that the performance is well-balanced. The excellent level of generalization ability was outlined by an overall accuracy of 99% for all classes of disease; it can be noted that Bacterial Canker and Phoma Blight had a precision of 97.01% and recall of 97.30%, respectively. The support values ranged from 1,445 for Sooty Mold to 1,530 for Black Tip dataset is fairly well spread. Support ratios were maintained at around 0.14 to 0.15 by each of the classes, thus pointing toward a significant enough presence of instances. Thereby, results produced reveal only the effectiveness of the model in anticipating and classifying cases of mango leaf diseases with accuracy but at the same time throw light on the imperative this model may have in the realm of agriculture for mechanisms to be chosen well in time for disease management. This development in predictive models presents a power tool for mango growers by promising healthier and higher crops.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Architecture for Context-Aware Tamil Text-To-Speech Synthesis with Multilingual Scalability
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The morphological abundance and high contextuality of Tamil, it is extremely challenging for Text-To-Speech (TTS) synthesis. This paper introduces a new Deep Neural Architecture for Context-Aware Tamil TTS Synthesis that improves intelligibility, naturalness, and multilingual flexibility through three major innovations: Multilingual Phoneme Embedding Network (MPEN) for better phoneme prediction from cross-lingual features, Prosody-Aware Transformer (PAT) for tone variation modeling and context-aware intonation, and Hybrid Spectrogram-Waveform Generator (HSWG) based on WaveNet and HiFi-Gan for high-fidelity speech synthesis. The resulting system achieves 98% intelligibility and 97.5% naturalness, surpassing state-of-the-art systems like Tacotron 2 and HiFi-Gan. The Mean Opinion Score (MOS) test verifies that the produced speech is extremely natural and human-like, and prosodic errors were decreased by 33% when compared with the older Tamil TTS models. Additionally, the model can be extended to other Indic languages and utilized in assistive technologies, AI-based voice assistants, real-time translation, and multilingual speech synthesis. The findings show that the system is efficient, scalable, and linguistically accurate, which is a valuable contribution to Tamil speech technology.

articleTitle: Forecasting Meteorological Drought Using Weather Data With a Machine Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Natural calamities like drought are severely impacted by the unpredictability of climate change and its adverse consequences. Drought is one of the major calamities that impact the social, economic, and environmental spheres across the globe. This necessitates accurate prediction methods to mitigate their effects. In order to forecast drought using meteorological data, this paper investigates a variety of machine learning methods, ranging from simple to intricate algorithms. The study focused on exploring the capabilities of feature selection and data balancing techniques to attain better scores. Among the different models, Random forest when combined with SMOTE achieved an accuracy of 0.82,while stacking approach emerged as the most effective with an accuracy of 0.83 and F1-score of 0.71. These findings underscores the importance of machine learning frameworks to tackle the challenges posed by drought and take proactive methodologies to mitigate its adverse impacts.

articleTitle: Advanced Face Detection Using SVM and Haar-like Features: A Comprehensive Approach in AI and Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Face detection is a vibrant research field spanning artificial intelligence, image processing, video surveillance, human-machine interaction, identity authentication, machine learning, pattern recognition, and so on. While humans effortlessly recognize faces, computers face challenges due to facial variability. The complexity lies in factors like expressions, lighting changes, and head positions. Thus, solving the problem of face detection has an important academic value and provides important enlightenment. There are many aspects to face detection such as facial expression, head position, changing lighting conditions and many others. To deal with face detection problems various approaches are used such as template matching methods, knowledge-based methods, feature invariant methods, and appearance-based methods. The proposed approach for face detection utilizes Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Haar-like Features. It begins by generating an integral image from a binary image measuring 19 x 19 pixels. Following this, the Haar feature extraction method is employed to obtain Haar values from both face and non-face isommages. A set of 200 face and non-face images from MIT database have been used. Features have been reduced five times to make different features sets of images. These features are passed to Support Vector Machine as input parameters and processed to classify face and non-face datasets. Support Vector Machine is used to create, train and test the neural network. Features are extracted on MATLAB and further processed in SVM using NeuroSolutions tool. The results are evaluated based on two scenarios as varying number of images and features.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Approach for Diabetes Detection and Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Diabetes, is a group of metabolic disorders in which there are high blood sugar levels over a prolonged period. If it was possible to predict the chance of the development of the disease then more timely intervention might help reduce the extent to which the disease effects its victims and health care services. This study focuses on the use of Machine Learning (ML) algorithms in analyzing patient data for the purpose of predicting diabetes risk. The Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, K-Nearest neighbors, Random Forest, Gradient Boost, Naive Bayes and XGBoost algorithms were employed to classify diabetes status, leveraging demographic and clinical features from a dataset of patient records. Each model’s effectiveness was assessed through preprocessing steps such as encoding categorical variables (e.g., gender and smoking history) and scaling numerical attributes (e.g., age, BMI, blood glucose levels). These classifiers have been evaluated using metrics which included accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score to gain the predictive performance and generalizability. Among all the models, Gradient Boost and XGBoost classifiers demonstrated the highest accuracy having 86% and 0.85 and robustness which makes them highly suitable for clinical decision-making applications in diabetes diagnosis and management.

articleTitle: Bit-Heart: Wearable Device for Healthcare Diagnosis Employing IOT and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: In this rapidly changing world, timely and cost-effective medical diagnosis is of utmost importance. This article introduces BitHeart, an IoT-based wearable device that tracks health events over time by combining wearable technology with machine learning models. This study proposes two models: first Heart Health Model which is employing IoT sensors such as heart rate monitors, accelerometers, etc. and the K Nearest Neighbor (KNN) method to predict the probability of heart disease based on physical measurements, include heartbeat rate, step count, and calories burned. Another is the body fitness model driven by a classifier called Gradient Boosting Classifier (LightGBM) is used in the evaluation of the patient by examining parameters such as step count, number of thoughts, weight and sleep duration. The hybrid technology processes the data to eliminate uncertainty and increase accuracy. The web-based interface allows users to view health data in real time and gain insights. Experimental studies have shown that the heart health model has 77% accuracy, while the physical health model can classify functional levels with high confidence. These results demonstrate BitHeart’s potential to improve personalized healthcare by providing users with early disease detection and recommendations.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Stock Movement Prediction: A Case Study of Hindenburg Research's Impact on Adani Group and Nifty-50
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The Nifty 50 index is a benchmark for the Indian stock market that calculates the average worth of the top 50 global companies listed on the National Stock Exchange (NSE). These 50-companies stock price momentum directly affects the Nifty 50 Index. In this work, Adani Enterprises (ADANIENT) and Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ld. (ADANIPORTS) stock datasets are used to train the proposed model. In addition, this letter gives a review of the Hindenburg research report (i.e., sentiment based) and its short selling in the Adani group. Due to short selling in ADANIENT and ADANIPORTS, t h e Nifty 50 was affected and came under a downtrend. The dataset used from December 2022 (1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> week) to March 2023 (2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> week) on a 1-hour time stamp in image form, and for the image scrap, tradingview.com have been considered. Based on three experts' opinions, the dataset is classified into three categories: holding position, bearish, and bullish. MACD, BB, and candlestick pattern indicators use to make the dataset. The dataset is made for ADANIENT, ADANIPORTS, and the Nifty 50 Index. It is trained on the SCNN model and Inception V3 pre-trained model with a dropout layer. SCNN model used a categorical cross-entropy loss function and Adam optimizer. In result analysis, the model attained validation accuracy of 97% for ADANIENT, 95% for ADANIPORTS, and 94% for the Nifty 50 Index.

Author Keywords: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ld. (ADANIPORTS)

articleTitle: Respond User Mindset for Enhanced VR Experiences: Integrating GSR Sensors with Virtual Reality Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: The goal of the virtual reality (VR) industry is to improve the experience of being physically present in a nonphysical environment a phenomenon known as VR immersion. To improve VR immersion, sound, simulators, and surrounding environments can be combined in a harmonious way. The virtual reality business is predicted to rise to approximately $26.89 billion by 2022 as a result of the technology's rapid expansion. However, due to its widespread spread and deep integration into daily life, a number of health problems, such as nausea, vomiting, vertigo, and cold sweats, have been documented. This paper proposes the integration of a Galvanic Skin Response (GSR) sensor with Virtual Reality glasses to predict the users emotional state. In addition, choosing the kind of virtual environment is a crucial component that significantly influences the user's heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, and oxygen saturation (SpO2). The GSR sensor measures changes in skin conductance, providing insights into the user's emotional arousal level. By analysing these physiological responses in real-time, the VR system can dynamically adjust environmental stimuli to evoke desired emotional responses or tailor experiences to individual preferences. The primary insights of the investigation illustrate that when an environment changes from a pleasant one to a frightening one, there is a noticeable difference in the quantity of skin conductance and immersion level. The overall mean values for all physiological factors increased from the pre-phase to post-phase of VR usage. The paper outlines the conceptual framework, potential benefits, and ethical considerations of this novel approach.

articleTitle: Autoregressive Diffusion Networks for Trustworthy Node Identification and Optimized Routing in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: Finding and eliminating unwanted nodes is a foremost challenge in wireless sensor networks (WSNs). This paper proposes an Autoregressive Diffusion Network (ADN) to find and categorize the nodes in the network as affected or trustworthy. Here, the proposed ADN provides a strong foundation for finding uncommon or insecure actions by effectively recording the characteristics of the sensor over a period of time. Thus, using the capability to capture successive data. In addition, an improved routing mechanism is developed using the Low-Energy Adaptive Clustering Hierarchy (LEACH) protocols. Then, the Pelican Optimisation Algorithm (POA) is used to optimize the cluster heads optimally. To further improve the routing mechanism using fitness proportional selection technique to transfer the data safely and effectively. Simulation results show that the proposed technique enhances the performance by reducing energy consumption and increasing the detection accuracy of affected nodes. The proposed LEACH + POA + ADN model shows the improved detection accuracy of 77%, false positive rate of 7.50%, average energy consumption of 8.02 J, network lifetime of 92.94 rounds, and packet delivery ratio of 92.97%, which is high compared to other benchmark models.

articleTitle: A Scalable Deep Learning Framework for Early Detection of Poultry Diseases Using Faecal Imagery
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Computation & Computer Technologies (InCACCT)
abstract: A major sector of agriculture, chicken farming delivers world-wide essential proteins.
